Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026-introduced

गृह मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री नित्यानन्द राय) : महोदय, मैं माननीय गृह मंत्री, श्री अमित शाह जी की ओर से यह प्रस्‍ताव करता हॅूं कि विदेशी अभिदाय (विनियमन) अधिनियम, 2010 का और संशोधन करने वाले विधेयक को पुर:स्थापित करने की अनुमति दी जाए ।

माननीय सभापति: माननीय सदस्‍यों, इससे पहले कि मैं माननीय गृह और सहकारिता मंत्री को विदेशी अभिदाय (विनियमन) अधिनियम, 2026 के पुर:स्‍थापित करने के लिए आग्रह करूं, मुझे सदन को सूचित करना है क‍ि माननीय गृह और सहकारिता मंत्री ने दिनांक 24, मार्च, 2026 के पत्र द्वारा सूचित किया है क‍ि माननीय राष्‍ट्रपति महोदया को प्रस्‍तावित विधेयक की विषय सामग्री से अवगत करा दिए जाने के बाद माननीय राष्‍ट्रपति महोदय ने संविधान के अनुच्‍छेद 117, क्‍लाज़ 1 के अंतर्गत लोक सभा में विधेयक को पुर:स्‍थापित करने की सिफारिश की है । 

प्रस्‍ताव प्रस्‍तुत हुआ: 

?विदेशी अभिदाय (विनियमन) अधिनियम, 2010 का और संशोधन करने वाले

विधेयक को पुर:स्थापित करने की अनुमति प्रदान की जाए ।?

SHRI MANISH TEWARI (CHANDIGARH): Mr. Chairperson, Sir, under Rule 72(1) of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, I rise to oppose the introduction of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 on multiple grounds enunciated hereunder. 

First, the Bill suffers from excessive delegation of essential legislative functions. Core aspects such as the manner of vesting, management disposal of assets, timelines, exemptions, and even appellate structures are left to be prescribed by the Central Governments through rules. 

This effectively reduces Parliament to enacting a skeletal framework contrary to the settled constitutional principles that essential legislative policy must be determined by the Legislature itself. 

Second, the Bill enables wide and unguided Executive control over property, including provisional and permanent vesting of assets in a designated authority with powers of management, transfer, and disposal. This raises serious concerns under Article 300A of the Constitution of India, as deprivation of property must be fair and accompanied by adequate safeguards, none of which are meaningfully embedded in the statute.

Third, the Bill concentrates adjudicatory, executive, and quasi-judicial powers in the same authority with limited and conditional avenues of appeal. This undermines the principles of natural justice and separation of powers, risking arbitrary decision-making. 

Fourth and final, the provisions enabling takeover, management, and disposal of assets, even where partly funded by non-foreign sources, are manifestly disproportionate and may have a chilling effect on legitimate civil society activity, thereby undermining the constitutional guarantee under Article 19(1)(c) of the Constitution of India, which is a fundamental freedom and a fundamental right.

In sum, the Bill perpetuates sweeping, unguided, and disproportionate powers in the Executive, without adequate safeguards or legislative clarity. It is, therefore, constitutionally suspect and ought not to be introduced in this House in its present form. Therefore, I oppose the introduction of this Bill. 

ADV. GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI (NANDURBAR): Sir, the State takeover of NGO assets amounts to quasi-expropriation and the proposed Bill centralises significant powers in the hands of the Central Government by allowing it to determine timelines for the use of foreign contributions, regulate the management of assets, and control over various NGO functionings. This is in violation of Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(c) as well. The experts and policy commentators have observed that the amendment may further shrink the democratic space available to civil society organisations. NGOs engaged in human rights, tribal welfare, public health, and education are likely to face heightened scrutiny, regulatory uncertainty, and fear of punitive action. 

While foreign contributions to NGOs are subjected to stringent controls, foreign direct investment in corporate sector continues under relatively liberal frameworks. This is again in violation of Article 14 of the Constitution of India. Also, I would like to say that this adversely impacts the charitable work of the vulnerable communities, and there is an impact on religious and minority institutions. Concerns have been raised by various religious and charitable organisations, including church bodies, regarding the potential impact of amendments on faith-based institutions. This is clearly in violation of Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution. Therefore, I object the introduction of this Bill.

SHRIMATI PRATIMA MONDAL (JAYNAGAR): I express my objection of the presentation of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment Bill, 2026, because of two reasons. One, this is a draconian Bill. By giving complete control of the authority to the Union Government, the Bill centralises disproportionate authority in the Executive, weakening institutional checks and federal balance, making it a violation of the basic structure of the Constitution. There is no independent oversight mechanism raising risk of arbitrary action. 

Two, the requirement of prior approval of the Union Government before initiating criminal proceedings under the Act introduces an element of Executive filtering, while it may act as a safeguard against arbitrary prosecution. It also centralises authority and unchecked discretion without the Union Government. I, therefore, oppose the introduction of this Bill.

श्री नित्यानन्द राय : महोदय, इस संशोधन विधेयक के संबंध में मैं बहुत संक्षिप्‍त में कहना  चाहूंगा । मुझे ऐसा लगता था कि यह बहुत आवश्‍यक संशोधन विधेयक है । यह सेवा के लिए, पारदर्शिता के लिए, नियम के अनुपालन के लिए भी और देशहित में थी । इसलिए इसका विरोध नहीं होगा, फिर भी विरोध किया गया है ।? (व्यवधान) मैं इनको यह जरूर कहना चाहूंगा कि अधिनियम के क्रियान्‍वयन के दौरान यह अनुभव किया गया कि प्रावधानों में कुछ अस्‍पष्‍टता है, जिसके कारण प्रशासनिक कठिनाइयां और प्रक्रियात्‍मक असंगतियां भी उत्‍पन्‍न होती रहती हैं । यह आवश्‍यक हो गया था कि एक स्‍पष्‍ट, संतुलित एवं क्रियान्‍वयन-उन्‍मुख विधिक व्‍यवस्‍था स्‍थापित किया जाए, जो प्रभावी परिवर्तन सुनिश्चित करते हुए संस्‍थाओं के लिए पारदर्शी एवं उत्‍तरदायी ढांचा प्रदान कर सके । यह इसका उद्देश्‍य है । फिर भी जो विरोध किया गया है और माननीय मनीश जी के द्वारा जो बातें कही गयी हैं । उन्‍होंने चार आपत्तियां दर्ज करायी हैं । मैं माननीय सदन को बहुत स्‍पष्‍ट रूप से बताना चाहूंगा कि विधेयक में निहितकरण, परिसंपत्तियों के प्रवर्धन एवं उपयोग के लिए मूल नीति एवं सिद्धांत अधिनियम में ही निर्धारित किए गए हैं । यह अलग नहीं हैं, जबकि प्रक्रियात्‍मक एवं क्रियान्‍वयन संबंधी पहलुओं को नियमों के माध्‍यम से विनियमित करना एक स्‍थापित विधायी अभ्‍यास है । 

दूसरा, विधेयक में अस्‍थायी एवं स्‍थायी निहितकरण के बीच स्‍पष्‍ट भेद किया गया है । जिसमें संस्‍था को अपनी स्थिति नियमित करने का अवसर प्रदान किया गया है तथा पात्र होने पर परिसंपत्तियों की वापसी का प्रावधान भी सुनिश्चित किया गया है । 

तीसरा, नामित प्राधिकरण को दिए गए अधिकार, विधेयक के भीतर निर्धारित शर्तों एवं नियंत्रणों के अधीन है तथा उनके निर्णय न्‍यायिक समीक्षा के अधीन रहते हैं । जिला न्‍यायालय में अपील का विशिष्‍ट प्रावधान भी किया गया है । जांच के लिए पूर्व स्‍वीकृति का प्रावधान, दुरुपयोग को रोकने हेतु एक संस्‍थागत सुरक्षा उपाय है न कि प्रवर्तन को बाधित करने हेतु । साथ ही विधेयक का उद्देश्‍य वैध गतिविधियों को प्रभावित करना नहीं, बल्कि विदेशी अभिदाय के उपयोग को पारदर्शी एवं उत्‍तरदायी बनाना है । 

महोदय, विदेशी अभिदाय अधिनियम का उद्देश्‍य यह है कि देश की सेवा में या जो माननीय जी.के. साहब ने चिंता व्‍यक्‍त की है, कोई भी शैक्षणिक संस्‍था या कोई भी एनजीओ, जो जन-सेवा करना चाहेगा, जिसका उद्देश्‍य देश की भावनाओं की संप्रभुता और अखंडता के अनुरूप होगा और जो भारत के संविधान और कानूनों के अनुरूप होगा, उसको बाधित करना नहीं है । लेकिन, मैं यह भी स्‍पष्‍ट करना चाहता हूं कि जो भारत के संविधान की भावनाओं, कानूनों और देशहित से अलग होकर काम करना चाहेगा, तो यह मोदी सरकार है । यह उसको बर्दाश्‍त नहीं करेगी । हम उस पर कानून के तहत कार्रवाई भी करेंगे । 

अभी प्रतिमा मैडम ने भी प्रश्‍न किया और कहा कि यह खतरनाक है । यह खतरनाक उनके लिए है, जिनकी नीयत में खोट होगी । ? (व्यवधान) जो विदेशी अनुदान और सहयोग लेकर यहां अवैध रूप से धन परिवर्तन करना चाहे, जबरदस्‍ती करना चाहे या छल करना चाहे या उस अभिदाय के माध्‍यम से अपने परिवार को या अपनी संस्‍था को जो निजी लाभ पहुंचाना चाहे, उसके लिए यह जरूर खतरनाक है । ? (व्यवधान) यह संस्‍थागत नियमों का उल्‍लंघन नहीं है । इसलिए मेरा इस सदन से अनुरोध है कि यह सदन विधेयक का समर्थन करे । 

इन्‍हीं शब्‍दों के साथ मैं इस विधेयक को सदन के विचारार्थ प्रस्‍तुत करता हूं ।

श्री लुम्बाराम चौधरी (जालौर) : माउंट आबू विश्व स्तरीय प्रसिद्व पर्यटन स्थल हैं । ब्रह्माकुमारी समाज का अंतराष्ट्रीय मुख्यालय माउंट आबू है । वर्ष मे लगभग 20 लाख से ज्यादा अनुयायियों पूरे विश्व से माउंट आबू आते हैं इन अनुयायियों को हवाई सफर के लिए 228 कि0मी0 दूर जोधपुर या 231 कि0मी0 दूर अहमदाबाद जाना पडता है । शक्ति पीठ अम्बा जी माता मंदिर आबू रोड से मात्र 20 कि0मी0 दूरी पर स्थित है । अम्बाजी में लगभग पाँच से छः लाख की संख्या में भक्तगण यहां आते है । यहां सात औद्योगिक क्षेत्र आबू रोड, अम्बाजी, मंडार, स्वरूपगंज, शिवगंज, सिरोही और पिंडवाडा हैं । बिनानी सीमेंट, लक्ष्मी सीमेंट, तिरूपति फाइबर, गुजरात केबल आदि आठ बडी 12 मध्यम एवं 2982 लघु उघोग स्थापित हैं । जालोर मे लगभग 3000 से ज्यादा ग्रेनाइट कटाई और प्रसंस्करण इकाइयां हैं । इस क्षेत्र से वायु सेवा प्रारंभ करने से जिले का त्वरित विकास होगा । अतः उड़ान योजना के अंतर्गत मानपुर हवाई पटटी से हिंडन हवाई अडडा तक वायुयान सेवा प्रारंभ किया जाए ।

श्री रुद्र नारायण पाणी (धेन्कानल) : राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 5 का कार्य अविलंब और ढंग से प्रारम्भ किया जाय । ओड़िशा के दो नंबर के नदी ब्रह्मणी मे तालचर से राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग संख्या 5 प्रारंभ किया जाने का विचार लगभग इस शताब्दी के शुरू से चर्चा मे हैं । इस बार वितमंत्री जी के बजट भाषण मे यह विषय प्रमुखता से उल्लिखित है । समल बैराज से धामरा/पारादीप तक यह जलमार्ग कार्य करने की धारणा लोगों में बनी हुई है । स्वर्गीय श्री अटल बिहारी जी की सरकार के समय से इसके बारे मे चिंतन चालू हुआ है । अब तो वास्तविक कार्य प्रारंभ किये जाने का समय आ गया है । इस मार्ग में ब्राह्मणी नदी में जो भी पुल अब बनाए जाने का विचार है उसको उसी ऊँचाई से बनाने का विचार चालू हो जाना चाहिए । काम तेजी से चालू होना चाहिए । दोनों किनारे के लोगों को इस परियोजना के सम्पूर्णीकरण में सम्पर्क किया जाना चाहिए । जलमार्ग की यह परियोजना होने से स्थल मार्ग में ट्रक परिवहन से काम चलाने वाले जो लोग प्रभावित होंगे उनको भी अग्राधिकार दिया जाना चाहिए ।

श्रीमती कलाबेन मोहनभाई देलकर (दादरा और नागर हवेली) : मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र दादरा और नागर हवेली में भारी वर्षा होती है, फिर भी गर्मियों के आते ही यहाँ के ग्रामीण और शहरी क्षेत्रों में पीने के पानी की भारी किल्लत हो जाती है । ​दमनगंगा नदी और मधुबन बांध के निकट होने के बावजूद, बुनियादी ढांचे और वितरण प्रणाली की कमी के कारण स्थानीय निवासियों, विशेषकर जनजातीय क्षेत्रों में माताओं-बहनों को पानी के लिए लंबी दूरी तय करनी पड़ती है । कई गांवों में जलस्तर काफी नीचे चला गया है और जल संचयन की उचित व्यवस्था न होने से जलसुरक्षा का संकट खड़ा हो गया है । अतः मेरा जल शक्ति मंत्री से अनुरोध है कि 'जल जीवन मिशन' के तहत इस क्षेत्र के लिए विशेष बजटीय आवंटन किया जाए । पुरानी पाइपलाइनों को बदला जाए, नए जल शोधन संयंत्र स्थापित किए जाएं और चेक डैम का निर्माण कर भूजलस्तर सुधारने हेतु ठोस कदम उठाए जाएं ताकि मेरे क्षेत्र की जनता को स्वच्छ और पर्याप्त पेयजल सुलभ हो सके ।

श्री मनसुखभाई धनजीभाई वसावा (भरूच) : गुजरात में मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र भरूच के अंतर्गत ट्राइबल बेल्ट, जिसमें वालिया, झगड़िया तथा नेत्रंग आदि क्षेत्र आते हैं, वहाँ सिंचाई की सुविधा बहुत कम है । इसी ट्राइबल बेल्ट के अंतर्गत नर्मदा जिला है, जिसे भारत सरकार द्वारा (आकांक्षी जिला) घोषित किया गया है । इस जिले में उन्नत कृषि और पशुपालन ही आजीविका के एकमात्र विकल्प हैं, अतः यहाँ पर्याप्त सहायता उपलब्ध कराई जानी चाहिए । इस क्षेत्र में, खासकर डेडियपाड़ा और सागबारा में सिंचाई की बिल्कुल सुविधा न होने के कारण लोग रोजगार के लिए पलायन करते हैं । सिंचाई की सुविधा हेतु डेडियपाड़ा क्षेत्र में गंगापुर डैम की तत्काल आवश्यकता है । मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र में कर्जन डैम अभी कार्यरत है, लेकिन वहाँ पानी की उपलब्धता कम है । अतः इन दोनों डैम में नर्मदा डैम का पानी लिफ्ट करके सिंचाई की सुविधा को सुगम बनाया जा सकता है । गुजरात बॉर्डर से लगे हुए ट्राइबल बाहुल्य वाले पड़ोसी राज्यों, जैसे?मध्य प्रदेश, राजस्थान और महाराष्ट्र के लोगों की समस्याएँ भी एक जैसी हैं । इस संबंध में सरकार से मेरा आग्रह है कि गुजरात के साथ-साथ पड़ोसी राज्यों में भी बेहतर कृषि, सिंचाई और पशुपालन हेतु उचित व्यवस्था की जाए, ताकि इनके जीवन को तत्काल बेहतर बनाने के प्रयास शुरू हो सकें ।

Regarding need to expedite operationalization of approved Nari Adalats in Karnataka- Laid

CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA (DAKSHINA KANNADA): I seek to raise an important matter regarding the Nari Adalat initiative under Mission Shakti, a commendable step towards strengthening grassroots dispute resolution and women?s empowerment. As per the Government?s reply to my Unstarred Question, Nari Adalats have been introduced as a pilot initiative and are being implemented in a limited number of Gram Panchayats. These forums provide alternative dispute resolution, grievance redressal, counselling, and facilitate referrals to institutions such as One Stop Centres, Police Stations, and District Legal Services Authorities. While this is a progressive initiative, its limited geographical coverage restricts its full potential. Notably, although Nari Adalats have been approved for 10 Gram Panchayats in Karnataka, they are yet to be operationalised. Given the increasing need for accessible, community-based justice mechanisms, such platforms can play a transformative role in resolving disputes in a timely, culturally sensitive, and cost-effective manner. In this context, I urge the Government to expedite operationalisation of approved Nari Adalats in Karnataka, including Dakshina Kannada district, and consider phased expansion across all districts in India. This will deepen access to justice and advance women-led grassroots empowerment in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Regarding information about runways/airstrips measuring upto 1400 metres in operation and aircraft model compatible for such airstrips in the country- Laid

SHRI ANUP SANJAY DHOTRE (AKOLA): I would like to seek information about the runways or airstrips of 1400 metres or below in length currently in operation in India along with the types and categories of aircraft that are permitted to operate from a 1400-metre runway or below, including the specific aircraft models that are technically eligible to operate from such runways in the country. Further, the Ministry may provide the name of airlines presently operating flights from runways of 1400 metres or below, along with details of the destinations served and the frequency of regular air services operated by them. Additionally, the Ministry may clarify the Government?s plan to make the UDAN scheme more broad-based, particularly with regard to explicitly ensuring that smaller aircraft and shorter airstrips are not restricted under the scheme.
records.ls|LS18_S7_6357:
Regarding need to formulate a dedicated National Menopause Policy to Address related health concern among women in the country- Laid

SHRI P. P. CHAUDHARY (PALI): I wish to draw the attention of the Government to the urgent need for a comprehensive national policy and specialised healthcare framework to address menopause among women in India. As per Census 2011, approximately 96 million Indian women were aged 45 or older. This demographic is projected to rise sharply to 401 million by 2026. With life expectancy of 75 years, Indian women will spend nearly 30 years, or one-third of their lives in the postmenopausal stage. Despite this, menopause remains an under-recognised public health concern. Clinical data indicate that menopause significantly increases the risk of depression, hypertension, and cardiovascular diseases. While the Government?s focus on maternal and child health is commendable, the specific needs of peri-menopausal and menopausal women remain a critical gap in our health discourse. Currently, Menopausal Hormone Therapy (MHT) is one of the effective treatments; however, it is not covered under the Government?s flagship insurance program, AB-PMJAY. I, therefore, urge the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to formulate a dedicated National Menopause Policy focused on awareness and clinical sensitisation. I further request the Ministry to include menopause-related diagnostics and MHT under the AB-PMJAY cover to ensure that every woman can age with dignity and health.
records.ls|LS18_S7_6358:
Regarding need to expedite land acquisition process for construction and development of various national highways in Karnataka- Laid

SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY (UDUPI CHIKMAGALUR): The delays in the development of National Highways in Chikkamagaluru, the development of NH-173, a 26 km stretch from Mooguti village to Mudigere, facing significant delays. Although the technical bid has been opened, compensation has not been paid to most of the 262 farmers who have surrendered their land. The Revenue Department and Forest Department are delaying the process, pointing fingers at each other, resulting in a stalemate. As an MP, I have convened at least 10 meetings to resolve this issue, but the land acquisition process remains stalled. The district administration is responsible for allocating land for the national highway, and it is imperative that they expedite this process. Furthermore, the land acquisition process for the 27 km stretches of NH-373 in Chikkamagaluru and Belur has not even commenced. Additionally, the 29 km long NH-169 from Mala SK Border to Kerekate Thanigodu, which was upgraded in 1999, facing delays due to the requirement of replacement land in forest area. The District Administration Forest Department has not allocated the land, causing further delays. I humbly request you to issue an order to the Principal Secretary to the Government of Karnataka to expedite the land acquisition process for these National Highways.
records.ls|LS18_S7_6359:
Regarding need to expedite processing for completion of Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) Project at Chandikhol in Jajpur district, Odisha-Laid 

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB (CUTTACK): I wish to draw attention of the Government towards a matter of urgent national importance regarding delays in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) project at Chandikhol in Jajpur district of Odisha, especially in the context of escalating tensions in Iran that have heightened concerns over India?s energy security. The 4 million tonne SPR project, sanctioned in December 2018 at a cost of ₹8,743 crore, is crucial for strengthening India?s emergency crude oil storage capacity. At present, the country has an existing capacity of 5.33 million tonnes at Visakhapatnam, Mangalore and Padur, sufficient to meet the requirement of 10 days. The project at Chandikhol and the capacity expansion at Padur will increase the capacity to 21 days. However, the project has been significantly delayed due to non-execution of the lease deed and incomplete handover of around 400 acres of land. Additionally, illegal stone quarrying in the project area continues unabated, threatening its viability despite repeated representations by Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited. I urge the Union Government to immediately intervene, coordinate with the Government of Odisha to expedite land transfer, stop illegal quarrying, and fast-track the project in view of its strategic importance.

Regarding alleged irregularities in functioning of Krishi Vigyan Kendra in Jalgaon district, Maharashtra-Laid 

श्रीमती स्मिता उदय वाघ (जलगांव) : मैं कृषि एवं किसान कल्याण मंत्री जी का ध्यान महाराष्ट्र के जलगांव जिले में स्थित कृषि विज्ञान केंद्र से जुड़े एक गंभीर विषय की ओर आकर्षित करना चाहती हूँ । यह केंद्र किसानों को आधुनिक कृषि तकनीक, प्रशिक्षण और वैज्ञानिक मार्गदर्शन प्रदान करने के उद्देश्य से स्थापित किया गया है, ताकि किसान नई पद्धतियों को अपनाकर अपनी उत्पादकता और आय बढ़ा सकें । किन्तु खेद के साथ कहना पड़ रहा है कि इस केंद्र के कार्यकलापों को लेकर कई गंभीर अनियमितताओं के आरोप सामने आए हैं । मैंने स्वयं इस केंद्र का दौरा किया, जहाँ यह पाया गया कि किसानों को अपेक्षित सहायता और प्रशिक्षण पर्याप्त रूप से नहीं मिल पा रहा है । इसके अतिरिक्त Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) से प्राप्त सरकारी निधियों के दुरुपयोग, पुराने पेड़ों की अनधिकृत कटाई तथा केंद्र के ट्रैक्टर और अन्य उपकरणों के निजी उपयोग जैसी शिकायतें भी सामने आई हैं । अतः मैं मंत्री जी से आग्रह करती हूँ कि इस पूरे प्रकरण की निष्पक्ष जाँच कराई जाए और जो भी दोषी पाए जाएँ उनके विरुद्ध कड़ी कार्रवाई की जाए, ताकि किसानों के हित सुरक्षित रह सकें और यह केंद्र अपनी मूल जिम्मेदारी के अनुसार कार्य कर सके ।

Regarding Railway related issues of Jammu Parliamentary Constituency-Laid

श्री जुगल किशोर (जम्मू) : मैं माननीय रेल मंत्री जी ध्यान मेरे सस्दीय क्षेत्र के जम्मू रियासी में रेलवे विभाग से सम्बंधित निम्नलिखित नए विकास कार्य हेतु एवं जनहित में जुड़े महत्वपूर्ण मांगे आपके समक्ष रख रहा हूँ, कृपया विचार कर आवश्यक कार्यवाही करने की कृपा करें: 1. सांबा के गांव गुरहा सलाथिया में रेल ओवर ब्रिज के निर्माण 2. जम्मू के बजालता में ओवर ब्रिज के निर्माण 3. मनवाल स्टेशन पर फुट ओवर ब्रिज बनाया जाए 4. जम्मू मेल, टाटा मुरी और सियालदाह एक्सप्रेस जैसी ट्रेनें सांबा रेलवे स्टेशन पर इनका ठहराव बहाल किया जाए । 5. मनवाल रेलवे स्टेशन पर संपर्क क्रांति, जम्मू मेल और हेमकुंड एक्सप्रेस का ठहराव होना चाहिए । 6. सांबा जिले के गांव राया सुचेनी जो रास्ता central यूनिवर्सिटी को भी जाता है, जनसुविधा को देखते हुए रेल ओवर ब्रिज बनाने की मांग को स्वीकृत दी जाए l 7. किशनपुर में रेलवे लाइन के पास बहुत सी ज़मीन खाली पड़ी है उस ज़मीन का सदुपयोग करने हेतु उसपर पार्क एवं गार्डन बनाया जाए | 8. जम्मू स्टेशन और कटरा स्टेशन के प्लेटफार्म पर नए स्टाल्स लगए जाएंगे l इन स्टालों में स्थानीय लोगों को रोजगार देने का प्रावधान किया जाए ।

Regarding alleged irregularities in 'Har Ghar Jal' Scheme in Palamu Parliamentary Constituency, Jharkhand- Laid

श्री विष्णु दयाल राम (पलामू) : झारखंड सहित पलामू संसदीय क्षेत्र के अंतर्गत दोनों जिलें पलामू एवं गढ़वा में केंद्र सरकार की महत्वाकांक्षी ?हर घर जल योजना? के क्रियान्वयन में गंभीर अनियमितताओं, कागजी प्रगति एवं संभावित भ्रष्टाचार की ओर ध्यान आकृष्ट कराना चाहता हूँ । सरकारी अभिलेखों में पलामू जिले को 75-80 प्रतिशत से अधिक जलापूर्ति कवरेज वाला दर्शाया गया है, जबकि वास्तविक स्थिति अत्यंत चिंताजनक है । छतरपुर, चैनपुर, हुसैनाबाद एवं पांडू प्रखंडों के साथ-साथ गढ़वा जिले के कांडी, मझिआंव, भंडरिया, रमना एवं मेराल प्रखंडों के अधिकांश गांवों में या तो नल कनेक्शन निष्क्रिय हैं या फिर जलापूर्ति अत्यंत अनियमित है । कई स्थानों पर बिना स्थायी जलस्रोत के पाइपलाइन बिछा दी गयी है तथा अधूरी ओवरहेड टंकियों के बावजूद कार्य पूर्णता प्रमाण-पत्र जारी कर दिए गए हैं । परिणामस्वरूप हजारों परिवार आज भी हैंडपंप, कुओं एवं तालाबों पर निर्भर हैं, जबकि कागजों में योजनाएं पूर्ण दर्शायी जा रही हैं । ये दोनों जिले सूखा-प्रभावित एवं आकांक्षी होने के कारण पेयजल संकट और भी गंभीर है । अतः आपके माध्यम से जल शक्ति मंत्रालय, भारत सरकार से अनुरोध है कि इस योजना की उच्चस्तरीय जांच कराकर दोषियों पर कड़ी कार्रवाई सुनिश्चित की जाय तथा वास्तविक रूप से योजनाओं को पूर्ण कर आम जनता को शुद्ध पेयजल उपलब्ध कराने की कृपा की जाये ।
records.ls|LS18_S7_6363:
Regarding need for urgent intervention to expedite transfer of outstanding funds from Andhra Pradesh Power Finance Corporation to the Government of Telangana- Laid

SHRI CHAMALA KIRAN KUMAR REDDY (BHONGIR): I would like to bring to kind notice of the Government that at the time of Bifurcation of the AP State in 2014 the total outstanding bond amount of AP Power Finance Corporation was Rs. 5,894.60 crore. In this connection, liabilities were apportioned between AP and Telangana in the ratio of 59.54% and 40.46% respectively and as a result, amount shared between AP and Telangana stands out to be Rs. 2,385 crore and Rs. 3,509.60 crore respectively. Contrary to this provision, Government of Andhra Pradesh has allocated an excess liability of Rs. 1,052.70 crore to Telangana Power Finance Corporation Under such circumstances, Telangana Power Finance Corporation has under protest discharged a principal amount of Rs. 481.82 crore and an interest amount of Rs. 788.18 crore, totalling Rs. 1,270 crores up to August 2024. Later, the Government of Telangana requested for kind intervention of the Union Government for an amount receivable from AP Power Finance Corporation for transfer of funds worth Rs. 1270 crore to Telangana State. In this regard, the State Government of Telangana sent concerned project proposals to the Ministry which are pending for necessary action. Hence, keeping in view of the interests and the overall development of the Telangana State, I request Hon?ble Minister of Finance, through the Chair, to kindly intervene in the matter to take necessary steps in coordination with the concerned Ministry to expedite the transfer of funds worth Rs. 1,270 crores from AP Power Finance Corporation to the Government of Telangana.
records.ls|LS18_S7_6364:
Regarding need to reconsider the proposed divestment of IDBI in view of safeguarding the public interest and financial stability- Laid

SUSHRI PRANITI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE (SOLAPUR): IDBI, established in 1964 under the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, has played a pivotal role in shaping India?s financial ecosystem, nurturing key institutions and supporting national development. During the passage of the IDBI (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 2003, the then Finance Minister assured Parliament that Government shareholding would not fall below 51%, a commitment recorded by the Committee on Government Assurances and central to IDBI?s transition into a banking entity. The proposed disinvestment of a majority stake by the Government and LIC, along with transfer of management control, raises serious concerns. It risks undermining the public sector character of IDBI Bank, potentially affecting depositors, MSMEs, farmers, and over 20,000 employees. Valuable real estate assets originally allocated for public purposes may pass into private hands. Depositors currently benefit from implicit sovereign assurance, which could diminish significantly post-privatization. Priority sector lending, including support for MSMEs, agriculture, and education, may weaken under private ownership. Additionally, implementation of welfare schemes and reservation policies could be adversely impacted. In light of these concerns, the Government should reconsider the proposed sale and explore retaining majority ownership or merging IDBI Bank with a Public Sector Bank to safeguard national and public interest.

Regarding need to issue pending Soil Health Cards to farmers in Bhandara district, Maharashtra- Laid

डॉ. प्रशांत यादवराव पडोले (भन्डारा-गोंदिया) : मैं सरकार का ध्यान मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड योजना के क्रियान्वयन में हो रही गंभीर विफलताओं की ओर आकर्षित करना चाहता हूँ । 2015 में शुरू यह योजना मिट्टी परीक्षण के आधार पर किसानों को संतुलित उर्वरक उपयोग की सलाह देती है, पर भंडारा ज़िले में स्थिति चिंताजनक है । जिला स्तरीय ?दिशा? समिति की समीक्षा में सामने आया कि 25,730 किसानों के नमूने लिए गए, लेकिन अब तक केवल 10,253 किसानों को कार्ड जारी हुए हैं । यानी 15,000+ किसान, जिनकी जाँच महीनों पहले पूरी हो चुकी है, आज भी कार्ड से वंचित हैं । गंभीर यह कि एक निजी अधिकृत प्रयोगशाला ने 4,992 नमूनों की जाँच की, फिर भी एक भी कार्ड जारी नहीं हुआ और कोई दंडात्मक कार्रवाई नहीं हुई । दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार नमूना लेने के 30 दिनों में कार्ड मिलना चाहिए, जबकि कई मामलों में 6?8 महीने की देरी हो रही है । इससे किसान बिना वैज्ञानिक जानकारी के उर्वरक निर्णय लेते हैं, लागत बढ़ती है, उत्पादन घटता है और मिट्टी की उर्वरता प्रभावित होती है । अतः सरकार सभी लंबित कार्ड तुरंत जारी करे, लापरवाह प्रयोगशालाओं पर कठोर कार्रवाई करे, तथा कार्ड-आधारित कृषि परामर्श सुनिश्चित करे, जवाबदेही तय हो, ताकि योजना कागज़ी नहीं, वास्तविक लाभ देने वाली बने ।

Regarding issuance of ST certificate to people belonging to Dhanka Community in Sriganganagar district, Rajasthan- Laid

श्री कुलदीप इंदौरा (गंगानगर) : मैं सरकार के समक्ष संसदीय क्षेत्र श्री गंगानगर के जिला कलेक्टर कार्यालय हनुमानगढ़ के सामने ST (अजजा) प्रमाण-पत्र को लेकर धानका समाज द्वारा धरना /आंदोलन कर रहें लोगों की बात रखना चाहता हूँ । भारत सरकार ने काका कालेलकर की अध्यक्षता में समिति का गठन किया था । जिस‌में समिति द्वारा रिपोर्ट तैयार कर भारत सरकार को सौंप दी गई । भारत सरकार ने इस रिपोर्ट को वर्ष 1976 (सितम्बर) मे संसद में पेश किया और उसी दिन यह रिपोर्ट सर्वसम्मति से पारित हो गई व गजट नोटीफ‌केशन जारी हो गया । इस रिपोर्ट के अनुसार धानका, बावरिया एवं नायका जाति को अ.ज.जा. (ST) में शामिल कर लिया गया । परन्तु राज्य सरकार द्वारा धानका व धाणका की रिपोर्ट मांग कर प्रमाण-पत्र पर रोक लगा दी । सरकार को निर्देशित करे कि धानका जाति के लोगों को अपने अधिकार से वंचित ना करें ।

श्री राजीव राय (घोसी) : मऊ जिले में स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं की स्थिति काफी कमजोर है और उन्नत चिकित्सा सेवाओं की पहुंच बहुत सीमित है । क्षेत्र के लोगों की लंबे समय से मांग है कि मऊ में एम्स की स्थापना की जाए, ताकि बेहतर इलाज की सुविधा मिल सके । प्रस्तावित एम्स से मऊ के साथ-साथ आसपास के जिलों-बलिया, गाजीपुर और आजमगढ़ को भी लाभ मिलेगा । इसके अलावा बिहार के सीमावर्ती जिले जैसे बक्सर के लोगों को भी सुविधा मिलेगी । वर्तमान में पूर्वाचल का एकमात्र एम्स गोरखपुर में है, जो मऊ से 100 किलोमीटर से अधिक दूर है, जिससे मरीजों को लंबी दूरी तय करनी पड़ती है और वहां अत्यधिक दबाव बना रहता है । मऊ प्रमुख सड़कों के किनारे स्थित है, जहां जनसंख्या और यातायात अधिक होने के कारण सड़क दुर्घटनाएं भी ज्यादा होती है । लेकिन यहां गभीर चोटों के इलाज के लिए ट्रॉमा सेंटर जैसी विशेष सुविधाएं नहीं है, जिसके कारण मरीजों को वाराणसी या गोरखपुर ले जाना पड़ता है और इलाज में देरी होती है । मऊ में एम्स बनने से आपातकालीन चिकित्सा सेवाएं मजबूत होंगी, मृत्यु दर कम होगी और क्षेत्र का विकास भी होगा । इसके लिए परधा मिल की जमीन या अन्य उपलब्ध भूमि दी जा सकती है, या आवश्यकता होने पर हम स्वयं भूमि उपलब्ध कराने के लिए भी तैयार हैं । अतः जनहित में मऊ में एम्स की स्थापना को शीघ्र मंजूरी दी जाए ।

Regarding need to suspend the Holistic Development of Great Nicobar Island Project in view of grave environmental and social concerns- Laid

SHRIMATI PRATIMA MONDAL (JAYNAGAR): The Government has approved the Holistic Development of Great Nicobar Island Project, with an estimated investment of 92,000 crore, covering a transshipment port at Galathea Bay, in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands While projected as a strategic and economic initiative, the project raises grave environmental and social concerns. Official documents indicate that the project will require diversion of large tracts of pristine tropical rainforest, involving the felling of nearly 10 lakh trees, with independent experts warning of even higher ecological loss. Great Nicobar forms part of a globally recognised biodiversity hotspot, home to endemic birds, rare wildlife, and fragile marine ecosystems, including one of the most important nesting sites for endangered leatherback sea turtles. Scientists have cautioned that such ecological loss is irreversible and cannot be offset through compensatory afforestation elsewhere. The project also threatens the habitat and way of life of indigenous communities, particularly the Shompen and Nicobarese, and is located in a seismically active and tsunami-prone zone, raising serious long-term safety concerns. We demand an immediate suspension of on-ground activities and a comprehensive, independent review of environmental clearances, with all assessment reports placed before Parliament for scrutiny, before any further implementation is allowed.

Regarding need for pro-active measures to ensure safety, security and timely evacuation of Indian Nationals in West Asian countries- Laid

DR. T. SUMATHY ALIAS THAMIZHACHI THANGAPANDIAN (CHENNAI SOUTH): I bring it to the notice of the Government about the precarious condition of Indians living in UAE, Saudi Arabia, Dubai, Qatar and middle-east with constant fear due to the ongoing high-voltage Iran-Israel war. Over 9 million Indian expatriates live in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. Remittances from this workforce have been consequential for the Indian Economy. India received a record $130 billion in-remittances in 2024. GCC countries contributed around 40% of India's total remittance inflows constituting 4% of GDP. Any large-scale evacuation of the Gulf would-present a massive logistical challenge. Moving such a population quickly would require extensive coordination of flights, possible sea routes, and diplomatic clearances. Air space over Dubai and Abu Dhabi remained shut in the days following the strikes, and airports in the UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, and Kuwait were either closed or severely disrupted. For workers employed in construction, oil, healthcare, and services, sudden exits would involve legal and contractual complications. Effective communication to prevent panic and misinformation-among workers in the Gulf and their families in India-would be essential at every stage. The conflict has generated serious anxiety among Indian migrant workers. Even without direct exposure to violence, the uncertainty around missile attacks, airspace closures, and emergency restrictions has upended daily life. At home in India, families dependent on regular remittances and daily contact face compounding worry. When the Gulf burns, India bleeds. India faces the human and economic cost of a war it did not start and cannot control. I urge the Union Government to take all necessary steps on war-footing mode to ensure safety and security of one crore Indians living under the gloom of war.
records.ls|LS18_S7_6371:
Regarding need to approve the proposal to include a number of water bodies in Andhra Pradesh under Phase III of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)- Laid

SHRI LAVU SRIKRISHNA DEVARAYALU (NARASARAOPET): I would like to draw the attention of the Government to the urgent need to approve the proposal for inclusion of 297 water bodies across five districts of Andhra Pradesh, Palnadu, Ananthapur, Sri Satya Sai, Nandyal and Kurnool, under Phase-III (Lot-3) of the PMKSY-HKKP-RRR scheme for FY 2025?26. The proposal submitted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh and examined by the Central Water Commission covers restoration, renovation and revival of traditional tanks that are crucial for irrigation in drought-prone regions of the State. The project includes 92 water bodies in Palnadu, 28 in Ananthapur, 55 in Sri Satya Sai, 91 in Nandyal and 31 in Kurnool, with an estimated total cost of ₹285.56 crore. Revival of these tanks will help restore the irrigation potential of over 26,500 hectares, improve groundwater recharge, enhance water availability and support thousands of farmers dependent on tank irrigation. These districts fall within water-stressed regions where agriculture remains highly vulnerable to erratic rainfall. Timely approval of this proposal will significantly strengthen rural water security and agricultural productivity. I therefore urge the Government to approve the proposal and include these water bodies under the PMKSY-HKKP-RRR scheme at the earliest.

संसदीय कार्य मंत्री; तथा अल्पसंख्यक कार्य मंत्री (श्री किरेन रिजिजू) : माननीय सभापति जी, मुझे सदन को जानकारी देनी है कि हाउस के बिजनेस को लेकर बीएसी में लोक सभा और राज्‍य सभा में चर्चा हुई थी और कई मैम्‍बर्स ने सुझाव भी दिए थे । 

मैं मैम्‍बर्स के सुझावों के बारे में मिलाजुलाकर बताना चाहता हूं कि कल यानी 26 मार्च को कैलेंडर होलिडे है । इसके बाद 27 मार्च, शुक्रवार को गवर्नमेंट बिजनेस लेकर आएंगे । हमने प्राइवेट मैम्‍बर्स बिल को बाद में एजस्‍ट करने के लिए कहा है इसलिए 27 मार्च, शुक्रवार को सरकार बिजनेस लेकर आएगी । 

पहले हमने निर्णय किया था कि 28 मार्च, शनिवार और 29 मार्च, रविवार को सरकार बिजनेस लेकर आएगी और हाउस चलाएगी । अब मैं सूचना देना चाहता हूं क‍ि ओरिजनल कैलेंडर के मुताबिक शनिवार और रविवार होलिडे रहेंगे । 

इससे आगे का तय है क‍ि 31 मार्च, मंगलवार को महावीर जयंती है, छुट्टी है और बाकी एज़ प्रपोज्‍ड जैसे हमने कैलेंडर शेड्यूल किया था, वैसे ही चलाने का प्रपोजल है । धन्‍यवाद ।

records.ls|LS18_S7_6376:
Finance Bill, 2026- passed

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE; AND MINISTER OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS (SHRIMATI NIRMALA SITHARAMAN): Thank you very much. I take this opportunity to reply on the debate which has been held on the Finance Bill itself.

Sir, nation-building is a continuous process and it does not happen overnight. Every Budget, every Finance Bill that we have come up with is a step towards the ultimate goal of attaining Viksit Bharat by 2047 and fulfilling the aspirations of 140 crore Indian citizens. So, in this quarter of the 21st Century, India is actually moving forward with reform, not out of compulsion, which is what has happened earlier. Reform is not happening out of compulsion, but out of conviction with clarity, confidence, and commitment. India is riding on the ?reform express? under the leadership of hon. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and this Finance Bill of 2026-2027, therefore, rests on five clear principles. 

First, there is a trust-based tax administration that is being improved upon. Actually, we are reducing unnecessary hardship for honest taxpayers. You can see various aspects of it in my response to various questions and clarifications sought by Members. I will elaborate on it. Second, Sir, is the ease of living for common citizens. I was worried that some of our hon. Members have started mocking ease of living and ease of doing business. It is important that we continue with that process. Every citizen should feel that this country does not really make it difficult for him by doing compliances, by seeking permits, by seeking quota, by seeking licences for legitimate businesses. I thought it was from 1991 that all of us kept saying India has to become a lot more easy to live in, a lot more easy to govern. So, it was astonishing for me to hear some Members talk about ease of living and ease of doing business as not so significant, not so important. I think it is important that we go on that route and make India a lot more easy to live in. 

Sir, third principle: we are empowering the MSMEs, farmers, and cooperatives because MSMEs, farmers, and cooperatives are at the heart of creation of employment for production and for overall development of India. So, this Finance Bill supports them with very many measures that improve liquidity but also reduce the compliance burden and give them the opportunity to have greater contribution made towards first their cooperatives and then the larger economy.

Fourth one is making India a stronger global business hub. That is why we have brought a clarity in very many provisions, particularly taxation-related provisions, which I will elaborate upon. These measures support key sectors such as digital infrastructure, electronics manufacturing, marine products, leather, critical minerals, nuclear energy, and so on ? all of which are critical for India to speed up towards Viksit Bharat.

The fifth and the final one is to enable seamless trade facilitation and bring in customs reforms. A number of provisions have been modified so that we are able to provide greater ease in trade facilitation. With these opening remarks on the Finance Bill itself, I will now, while responding to the hon. Members, elaborate on some of the features contained in the Bill.

To begin with, the hon. Member from the Indian National Congress, Dr. Amar Singh ? whom I respect greatly, as he is a trained economist and has served as the head of the Planning Commission in Punjab, and has contributed to debates in this House ? this time, I felt, did not speak as an economist. He spoke more like a politician seeking to take a potshot at the ruling party. I wish he had contributed to the debate with his wisdom and his exposure to the field of economics. What he said, however, astonished me. It could not have come from him, but since he has said it, I must respond. I am only summarising. He mentioned that there is nothing in this for the middle class, and that everything has been done for big businesses. What an irony! I believe this Finance Bill has much more for the middle class. If I were to list a few measures, I hope Dr. Amar Singh will concede that he was on a completely wrong track.

This Finance Bill has slashed the TCS rate for remittances made for education and medical purposes under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, popularly known as LRS. It was earlier five per cent; we have brought it down to two per cent so that people who send money abroad for their children ? middle-class families who often borrow for this purpose ? have a lower TCS burden. Similarly, TCS on overseas tour packages, where people travel in groups, families together and so on, was earlier 20 per cent; it has now been reduced to two per cent. Are large corporates undertaking such group tours? No, ordinary middle-class families do. I would like to draw his attention to this.

Second, we have completely exempted basic customs duty on 17 critical life-saving drugs and medicines. Will this not benefit small families and ordinary citizens whose family members are hospitalised and who must purchase expensive medicines? We have reduced the basic customs duty to zero and fully exempted them. Furthermore, duty-free personal imports of medicines ? where children living abroad send medicines for upkeep of their parents, special food items, or medical nutrition for those undergoing severe treatment ? have been extended to cover seven additional rare diseases. These too are now eligible for duty-free personal imports. This will certainly benefit the middle class.

Similarly, any interest awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal ? for instance, when there is a delay in payment and the affected families are waiting for compensation ? was earlier taxable. That tax has now been completely removed. It is fully exempt. Will this not help families awaiting insurance payouts after such tragic incidents? We are also proposing to allow taxpayers to update their returns even after reassessment proceedings have been initiated. Normally, once such proceedings begin, corrections are not permitted. We have now allowed this, subject to an additional 10 per cent tax over and above the rate applicable for the relevant year.

So, the Assessing Officer will then use this updated Returns for further proceedings. It makes life easier for the taxpayer. 

Young professionals, students, and relocated NRIs often make inadvertent mistakes or errors in their assessment when they file it. A one-time six-month foreign assets disclosure for small taxpayer scheme has been brought in whereby this small taxpayer can declare small overseas assets which are left undeclared till then or even income up to Rs. 1 crore, if it has been left without disclosure and up to Rs. 5 crore of previously taxed but undeclared assets, are now without any prosecutions to be faced. They can just declare and do the due process. There will be no prosecution after that. This will bring in great relief for small taxpayers who by chance or did not know or inadvertently missed out on declaring amounts which are left in accounts abroad. 

Senior citizens and small savers will also benefit from a new single-window system allowing depositories to accept Forms 15G and 15H directly and distribute them to relevant companies ending the hassle of submitting multiple personal forms to avoid TDS on dividends. So, instead of the tax assessee paying it to so many different agencies, the depositories can do it on behalf of the tax payers, particularly the senior citizens. Therefore, this will be a relief. 

Now I come to a very important thing, which will affect all passengers, all relatives, families, friends, and even hon. Members who go abroad and come back. We are rationalizing the passenger allowances, rationalization in tariffs on gifts and also on personal imports and simplification of personal effects. This reduces disputes at the airports. I normally receive a huge lot of day-to-day complaints of, "I am held back in Delhi airport, the customs official is not letting me go. I am saying this is mine. They are saying, No, this is new?. All these disputes will now be over. We are increasing, in fact, we have rationalised it completely on every item that you can bring. If you want, you take it back or if you want, you leave it. So, passengers now will have far less to worry about when they land in India. 

Finally, digitization of temporary imports and exports of valuables including jewellery and professional equipment, bringing in cameras, going out with cameras, simplifies travel for individuals attending overseas events, medical procedures, and also on personal visits. So, if this is the set of relief that we are offering, these are aimed at offering for the middle-class, for the passengers, and ordinary citizens. It is not for those big travellers or high net-worth individuals. 

Similarly, for MSMEs, there are two principles which I would want to put upfront. We take this approach for dealing with MSMEs -- penalize first, do not take them to a criminal court or whatever. Actually, we are moving away from penalizing first and giving them the relief. One more thing that I would like to say is that we are facilitating first and enforcing later, if necessary. So, in that way, we are taking an approach which is friendly for MSMEs. Penalties for technical defaults like failing to get accounts audited have been converted into predictable fixed fees. So, there is no uncertainty that the MSMEs will have to face. 

Similarly, rule-based automated process for small taxpayers have been brought in to obtain a lower or nil deduction certificate online itself. 

So, there are very many more which I can list out, but the fact is that individuals or MSMEs have been given more facilitated treatment. 

For strengthening agriculture, fisheries and the cooperatives, there are several measures in this Finance Bill. Primary cooperative societies enjoy deduction for supplying milk, fruits and vegetables to their federal cooperatives. This Budget or this Finance Bill also expands that deduction to include cooperatives supplying cattle feed and also cotton seed, recognising the integrated nature of rural value addition. 

To build stronger cooperatives, and particularly cooperative federations, inter-cooperative society dividend income has been made tax deductible. So, under the new tax regime, provided it is further distributed to members, if the federal cooperative is going to pass the dividend further down to its members, under the new tax regime, this treatment will be offered.

Furthermore, a three-year tax exemption has been granted to dividend income received by notified national cooperative federation. All this is going to help small members in the cooperative societies. And similar treatment is being given to Indian fishing vessels in the Exclusive Economic Zone or on the high seas. They will now be completely free of customs duty. So, we want to facilitate first and enforce the law, if necessary, much later. That will simplify lives for cooperatives, fishermen, individuals and so on.

On the cesses and surcharges, every Session we have this question of why should cesses be collected, why should surcharges be collected, and because it remains outside of the divisible pool, it is not doing justice to the State. The Constitution makers knew what they were doing, and we all pay respects to them. There is a provision for levying cesses and surcharges which is given to the Central Government. We are using a provision which is legitimately provided to the Central Government. They say, ?Add that also into the divisible pool.? No, there is a provision for us to use it, we will use it. Just as there are several provisions given to the States to levy tax on certain items which has nothing to do with the divisible pool, do we question that? No. And therefore, repeated allegation that we are collecting cesses and surcharges, it should actually be going, oh sorry! Please read the Constitution again. We are allowed to do it and we are doing a legitimate thing. But having received it, having collected it, are we not spending it only on the States, providing hospitals, schools and laying the roads? In fact, I have said this every time, I am saying it now again. More than what is collected as cesses and surcharges is what we spend on schemes to the States. I will just go on reading the numbers and I hope the Members will understand those collected cesses and surcharges are not lying with us. It is actually going to the States.

The Samagra Shiksha Mid-Day Meal Scheme, implemented through State Governments is financed through the Health and Education Cess. 
 For the National Food Security Act, Centre bears the bulk of the cost and States distribute. 

Even in the recent Supplementary Demands for Grants which was passed in this House only a few days ago, Rs. 11,627 crore was transferred to PM Swasthya Suraksha Nidhi to meet National Health Mission expenditure. So, resources from many cesses are 100 per cent transferred to States. In fact, if it was part of the divisible pool, they would only get 41 per cent of it. So, I want to underline the fact that they are getting. In fact, 105 per cent utilisation has happened. We spend more than what we collect. 

For example, in the last six-year period from 2019 to 2024-25, the cumulative utilization of cesses has exceeded the collection, कितना कलेक्ट हुआ और कितना उनको भेजा गया? Rs.15.14 lakh crore were collected. कितना भेजा गया? Rs.15.97 lakh crore have been sent to the States under various schemes. So, more than what is collected under cesses and surcharges is being spent. I think repeatedly raising doubts about putting it in the divisible pool, not realizing that not 100 per cent, but only 41 per cent will reach you, is just making a lot of noise without understanding the details.

Similarly, in Health and Education Cess, Rs.74,000 crore extra has been spent over and above what has been collected under Heal and Education Cess. What was collected? Rs.7.03 lakh crore was collected and that is between 2014-15 to 2026-27. Against this, the total utilization stands at Rs.7.77 lakh crore. From Rs.7.03 lakh, it has gone up to Rs.7.77 lakh crore, which is Rs.74,000 crore extra. I think these replies should dispel the doubt about cesses and surcharges. 

A very important point was raised by Dr. Amar Singh that data centres lack requirements for localization, employment and technology transfer. So, giving them tax holidays is not good at all. This is the observation of Dr. Amar Singh. I would like to highlight that the Budget for 2026-27 has designed tax holidays with structural conditionalities and complementary skilling initiatives to ensure domestic value creation happens. The tax holiday until 2047 is available only when the foreign cloud provider utilizes data centre services located in India, meaning the physical infrastructure must be built and operated domestically. This guarantees that construction, operation, maintenance and also the jobs largely stay local. All sales to Indian users must be routed through an Indian reseller entity, creating an entire ecosystem of Indian system integrators, managing service providers and telecom partners who capture value and employment locally. This is absolutely clear. Therefore, this tax holiday is going to bring in investment, keep them here, create jobs here and utilize data services here and then also export. So, it is not as if this were all for somebody from outside and nothing for us. 

Even the safe harbour rule given in the Finance Bill ensures genuine Indian operations. The 15 per cent safe harbour margin on cost for resident Indian entities providing data centre services to related foreign companies ensures that Indian operations are not hollow shell but retain meaningful profit, and build genuine technical capability. So, this guarantees that Indian entities are adequately compensated for real work performed by local professionals. So, Dr. Amar Singh should remove that doubt from his mind. In fact, I would add one more point. USD 70 billion in data centre is already under way for investment and India?s cloud capacity is projected to grow four or five times by 2030. The sheer volume of construction, cooling infrastructure, power management, cybersecurity and network operations demanded will generate lakhs of direct and indirect jobs in India.

And about debt, which Manish Tewari Ji was saying that debt has risen from 56.51 lakh crore rupees in 2013-14 to 214.8 lakh crore rupees in 2025-26. Again when you are talking of debt, the Central Government alone cannot be responsible for debt. SHRIMATI PRATIBHA SURESH DHANORKAR (CHANDRAPUR): Hon. Chairperson, today, I rise in this House to speak on the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026. When this legislation was enacted in 2016, its primary objective was the timely revival of industries. However, in light of the experiences of the past decade, serious structural flaws have become apparent within this process.

13.56 hrs (Shrimati Sandhya Ray in the Chair)

Specifically addressing the issues of insolvency and the cooperative sector, I would like to cite the example from 2002 involving the districts of Buldhana, Wardha, and Osmanabad. Banks with a financial capacity of merely ₹100 crore extended loans amounting to as much as Rs.1,000 crore. Taking the Buldhana Central Bank as a case in point, its eventual insolvency was primarily the fault of its Board of Directors. They defrauded the bank by sanctioning loans to their own relatives and acquaintances. This crisis occurred because loans were disbursed far beyond the bank's actual capacity; while the funds involved represented the hard-earned savings?the very "sweat and toil"?of farmers, it was the farmers who ultimately bore the brunt of the loss. Yet, neither those who sanctioned the loans nor those who received them suffered even the slightest financial detriment. Approximately Rs.300 to Rs.700 crore of farmers' money was lost in this scandal?a bank scam orchestrated through a nexus involving the Board of Directors, bank officials, and political pressure. Consequently, farmers, small traders, and women belonging to self-help groups suffered massive financial losses. We deposit our savings in banks, often covered by deposit insurance schemes; under these provisions, for deposits up to Rs.5 lakh, the government is mandated to provide a refund to the depositors.

As we are all aware, the hon. Amit Shah currently holds the portfolio for the Ministry of Cooperation. Cooperation is not merely a subject for rhetoric; it represents an institution?a bond of trust and a relationship. Anyone who trifles with this sacred bond must be held accountable and punished. The money deposited in these banks belonged to farmers?individuals who had saved those funds by making immense personal sacrifices and enduring severe hardships. The funds belonging to women who sold their jewelry to save money?as well as the savings set aside for their daughters' weddings?remain frozen. My question to the government is this: For how much longer do you intend to conduct inquiries? For how much longer will you make the people suffer while the accused continue to roam free? The public's patience has run out. Consequently, this current calm is poised to transform into a storm. Even today, the people possess the power to overthrow this regime.

14.00 hrs

Punjab National Bank has faced a default of Rs.13,000 crore, a scandal in which the names of individuals like Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi feature prominently. The PMC Bank accepted deposits amounting to Rs. 6,500 crore and subsequently concealed these funds. Loans issued by HDIL Bank have also been hidden from public scrutiny. We have observed that these frozen assets included the life savings of pensioners and street vendors?amounting to thousands of crores of rupees. Similarly, YES Bank incurred liabilities amounting to thousands of crores, while ICICI Bank also accumulated debts worth thousands of crores before its key figures fled the country. The list of affected institutions also includes Lakshmi Vilas Bank, Global Trust Bank, Sahara Bank, and the Mumbai Cooperative Bank.

While the PMC Bank was embroiled in a scam worth thousands of crores, financial irregularities were also committed under the guise of the Maharashtra State Cooperative Sugar Industry. The fact that hundreds of crores remain trapped in the Buldhana State Cooperative Bank appears not to be a mere coincidence, but rather indicative of a systematic pattern being executed. It is imperative that we also investigate under whose patronage this organized racket of looting the public has been allowed to flourish. You claim that you will take action and, to that end, you constitute a committee; however, you must ask yourselves: Do you truly possess the courage to return the public's money? You owe the public an answer to this question.

Funds were looted through the banking system, leaving thousands of people unemployed, while the perpetrators fled with the stolen assets?amounting to crores of rupees belonging to millions of people. These stolen funds were subsequently channeled into the real estate sector, a practice that exacerbated the financial crisis and led to a surge in bankruptcies. I ask you to reflect upon this matter and state clearly: Do you intend to take concrete action? Regarding the Mumbai Cooperative Bank, allegations of large-scale corruption have surfaced, even leading to an uproar within the Legislative Assembly; yet, the individuals accused of these crimes have still not been arrested.

When small traders and farmers are unable to repay loans taken for their homes or businesses, we file criminal charges against them and initiate asset seizures. However, in the case of large-scale industries, we refrain from taking such action and instead allow the defaulters the liberty to travel abroad. I earnestly request that you view this matter with the utmost seriousness. Maharashtra serves as the engine of the nation's economy; however, this engine has stalled due to administrative delays. The Baijayant Panda Committee submitted a report in 2025, which outlined numerous recommendations for reform.

Under the IBC, it was expected that verdicts would be delivered within 180 days; yet, to date, no such verdicts have been pronounced. NCLT benches in cities like Mumbai and Nagpur are burdened with thousands of cases that have remained pending for years. This situation is causing significant distress for budding entrepreneurs across Maharashtra. The government should focus on devising strategies to ensure that the judicial process works to the advantage of these entrepreneurs?without necessarily altering existing laws. This government?which proclaimed that it would provide loan waivers for farmers?must answer for the multi-crore loan waivers it has actually granted to large industrialists. Furthermore, it must explain what steps it intends to take to recover these funds and when it plans to repatriate the individuals responsible back to India.

Why does the Central Government not demonstrate the same alacrity regarding the 2019 situation as it does in the corporate sector? The government enacted legislation specifically to combat fraudulent schemes; yet today, companies like the Sahara have gone bust. For the past ten years, ordinary citizens?who invested their hard-earned money in schemes like Maitreya and Sahara with the hope of enriching their lives?have received no returns. This crisis has disproportionately affected daily wage earners, rural families, and retired employees; despite facing severe hardships?even to the point of starvation?they have received no assistance. Tragically, some have been driven by desperation to end their lives; it is a cruel irony that they are unable to access the very investments they made to secure their future. This calamity has plunged thousands of families into financial peril and severely deteriorated their mental well-being. I earnestly request that you pay immediate attention to this matter and extend necessary assistance to these affected families.

Lakhs of hardworking citizens across Maharashtra have been financially ruined. Why are the funds seized by central agencies?such as the ED, CBI, and SEBI?not being handed over to the competent authorities designated to handle such matters? Just as you are currently implementing reforms within the IBC framework to facilitate the corporate sector, will this government provide an assurance that it will utilize the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act (BUDS Act) to ensure that ordinary victims and investors recover their money?

When a company goes bankrupt, the families of its employees are often left destitute. Regrettably, these workers frequently fail to receive their outstanding wages and Provident Fund (PF) dues. It is imperative to establish accountability for the agencies and officials responsible for this situation, particularly those who are deliberately causing delays in resolving these matters. I demand that this Bill should not merely serve the interests of suit-wearing industrialists, but must also safeguard the interests of banks, ordinary investors, small entrepreneurs, and workers. I urge you to ensure that these laws do not remain mere paper formalities, but are effectively utilized to deliver justice to the victims.

As I have stated previously, the Buldhana Urban Bank?along with other similar institutions?constitutes the very backbone of our rural economy. Therefore, while declaring insolvency, it is absolutely essential to prioritize and uphold the laws designed to ensure the security of ordinary depositors.

Today, the Central Government has written off the debts of 52 major industrialists. In the recently presented Union Budget, a staggering sum of Rs. 8 lakh crore was waved off. The government appears to have the funds to waive the loans of a select few industrialists, yet it claims to lack the resources to waive the loans of the farming community. Therefore, through this platform, I earnestly request that you give due consideration to the plight of our farmers; the agricultural sector in our state is currently facing a grave crisis. Farmers are driven to despair due to rising production costs, volatile market prices, natural calamities, and crop damage. Under these circumstances, a complete waiver of agricultural loans has become an absolute necessity.

As was highlighted earlier in the context of Mumbai, members of Self-Help Groups?particularly women?are working diligently and effectively through the medium of District Cooperative Banks. It is important to recognize that intelligence and capability are not confined solely to women in urban areas; women in rural areas are equally astute. They are performing their roles with great competence, empowered by the support extended to them through the District Banks. I further demand that we also give due consideration to the needs and concerns of small traders and street vendors.
