CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA (DAKSHINA KANNADA): I wish to speak on the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Railways.

First, I would like to commend the Government under the leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji and the Hon'ble Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw ji for the continued transformation of Indian Railways. Over the past decade, Indian Railways has undergone a historic modernization with record capital investment, expansion of electrification, station redevelopment under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, introduction of Vande Bharat trains, and a renewed focus on passenger comfort, safety, and logistics efficiency.

The Railway Budget for 2026-27 continues this strong momentum with a record allocation of around Rs 2.78 lakh crore for Indian Railways, with nearly Rs 2.93 lakh crore earmarked for capital expenditure, the highest ever investment in the sector. The Budget places a strong emphasis on capacity expansion through new lines, doubling, electrification and modern signalling, along with continued investment in station redevelopment under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme and upgradation of Vande Bharat trains.

I would also like to take this opportunity to thank the Ministry of Railways for an important development in my constituency of Dakshina Kannada.

The electrification of the Mangaluru - Sakleshpur railway route, including the challenging ghat section, is a significant step forward for rail connectivity in coastal Karnataka. This project improves operational efficiency, reduces dependence on diesel locomotives, and strengthens the vital Bengaluru Mangaluru rail corridor that serves thousands of passengers every day. I sincerely thank the Hon'ble Railway Minister and the Ministry for prioritizing this important infrastructure upgrade which greatly benefits the people of the region.

At the same time, I would like to place a few important requests before the Ministry which are critical for improving railway connectivity in Mangaluru and coastal Kamataka.

First, there is a strong case for introducing a Vande Bharat Sleeper Express between Mangaluru and Bengaluru. This is one of the busiest intra-state corridors in Karnataka with high demand from students. professionals, tourists, and traders travelling between the coastal region and the state capital. At present only a limited number of overnight trains operate on this route and they are frequently fully booked. A Vande Bharat Sleeper service would significantly improve connectivity and passenger comfort on this important corridor.

Second, there is a need to examine the feasibility of developing an additional city-centric railway station in Mangaluru. Currently trains arriving from the eastern side and proceeding northwards along the coastal corridor must deviate from their natural alignment to reach either Mangaluru Central or Mangaluru Junction. A well-located city-centric station on the east-west approach corridor would reduce detours, save travel time, and better serve the growing passenger demand in the city.

Third, I would also request the Ministry to consider reorganizing the railway administrative structure of Mangaluru by examining the feasibility of bringing it under the Mysuru division of South Western Railway instead of the current administrative control from Palghat. Given the geographical proximity and regional connectivity patterns, such a step would greatly improve administrative efficiency and accessibility for the people of coastal Karnataka.

Fourth, Sir, the Konkan Railway corridor remains one of the most important rail lifelines along the western coast of India. I would request the Ministry to consider the merger of Konkan Railway with Indian Railways, which would facilitate integrated planning and faster infrastructure expansion. Alongside this, doubling of the Konkan Railway line from Mangaluru onwards along the coastal corridor must be prioritised, as several stretches remain single line and act as capacity constraints for both passenger and freight movement. 

Fifth, I would also like to propose that the Government consider developing a High Speed Rail corridor between Mangaluru and Bengaluru, linking it with the upcoming Bengaluru - Chennai High-Speed Rail corridor. Such a corridor would create a powerful east-west economic link, connecting the western seaboard with southern India's major economic centres. Given that Mangaluru hosts the New Mangalore Port, one of the major commercial ports on the west coast, such connectivity would significantly strengthen passenger mobility. freight logistics, and port-led development.

Finally, I would request the Ministry to consider doubling the railway line between Mangaluru Central and Mangaluru Junction. Though this is a short section within the city, it has become a critical bottleneck because both stations handle long-distance passenger trains as well as freight traffic connected to the New Mangalore Port. Doubling this section would improve operational flexibility, reduce delays, and strengthen the overall efficiency of the railway network in coastal Karnataka.

Mangaluru is an important port city, an educational hub, and the economic gateway of coastal Karnataka. Strengthening railway infrastructure in this region will not only improve passenger mobility but also support port-led development, tourism, and regional economic growth.

I therefore request the Hon'ble Railway Minister to kindly consider these proposals in the larger interest of connectivity and development in Dakshina Kannada and coastal Karnataka.

Thank you. Jai Hind. 

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB (CUTTACK): Indian Railways is entering a phase where corridor-led capacity creation, freight efficiency and network reliability will drive investment decisions. The Economic Survey 2025-26, signalled a clear shift away from broad network expansion towards targeted throughput gains. The policy emphasis has moved to easing congestion on high density routes, improving freight movement and strengthening multimodal integration through Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) and economic rail corridors under the PM Gati Shakti framework. Dedicated freight infrastructure is central to this outlook. Of the planned 2,843 km DFC network, 2,741 km or 96.4 percent has been commissioned as of October 2025. The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor spanning 1337 km has been completed, while 1404 km of the 1506 km Western Dedicated Freight Corridor is operational. The corridors have reduced freight transit time and eased congestion on passenger routes. Under the PM Gati Shakti framework, three economic railway corridor programmes covering energy, mineral and cement routes, port connectivity and high traffic density lines have identified 434 projects with a total outlay of Rs 11.17 lakh crore. Of these, 122 projects covering 12,150 km have been sanctioned while 198 projects spanning 19,779 km are under various stages of appraisal. The corridors are intended to align rail capacity with freight demand and improve integration with ports, industrial clusters and logistics hubs. For the financial year 2026-27, allocation of Rs 2,77,830 crore is for capital expenditure. This allocation is for construction of new lines, procurement of locomotives, wagons and coaches and other infrastructure works. The Railways had received Rs 2,52,000 crore in 2025-26. The current allocation is a 10.25 percent increase, making it the highest ever capital outlay for the sector. In addition, the Railways will receive Rs 15,000 crore from Extra Budgetary Resources.Total earnings of the Railways are projected at Rs 3,85,733.33 crore while expenditure is estimated at Rs 3,82,186.01 crore resulting in a surplus of Rs 3,547.32 crore at the end of the financial year. Under the able leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian Railways is set to make rail travel in 2026 more comfortable, efficient and memorable through innovation and indigenization. With the common man at its core, the Railways has taken significant strides towards building a world class rail network. Seven new high speed corridors across India will bring top Indian cities closer. The South High Speed Diamond will benefit Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry. High speed rail corridors spanning about 4,000 km are expected to attract around Rs 16 lakh crore investment. A 2052 km long new Dedicated Freight Corridor announced between Dankuni in West Bengal and Surat in Gujarat will strengthen East-West trade.

As part of the long-term vision, the Government has announced the development of seven high speed rail project corridors between cities as "growth connectors" to promote environmentally sustainable passenger transport systems. These corridors include Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Bengaluru, Hyderabad-Chennai, Chennai- Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri. The proposed corridors are expected to significantly reduce inter-city travel time and facilitate seamless multimodal movement of passengers. With the announcement of the new corridors, the rail-based transportation ecosystem is expected to undergo a paradigm shift.

Recently, the Rail Minister highlighted record achievements in infrastructure creation including construction of 35,000 km of new tracks, 4,700 km of electrification and electrification coverage exceeding 99.5 percent of the broad-gauge network. Manufacturing of Vande Bharat sleeper and chair car trains, Amrit Bharat and Namo Bharat trains along with record induction of wagons is progressing at an unprecedented pace. As one is aware, rail transport is nearly 95 percent less polluting than road transport. The record allocation reinforces the role of Indian Railways as a backbone of national development, economic growth and inclusive connectivity.

Coming to Odisha, one may say this year's budget allocation is historic. During 2009-14, annual average allocation was around Rs 1000 crore or Rs 1,171 crore to be specific whereas in 2026-27 about Rs 10,928 crore has been allocated which is 13 times more to the earlier figure. At present, massive investment has been made. Total works worth Rs 90,659 crore are under progress. Track creation, station development and safety enhancement are taking place across the entire state of Odisha. A total of 59 stations of Odisha have been identified for redevelopment under the Amrit Station Scheme. For station modernization around Rs 2,439 crore is being invested and already 6 stations have been completed. The second entry of Cuttack station is one of them which was completed in record time and has been inaugurated. Other stations include Baripada, Barpali, Bimlagarh, Paralakhemundi and Talcher. Travel efficiency in the state has reached new heights with the expansion of premium train services such as 6 pairs of Vande Bharat Express and 6 pairs of Amrit Bharat Express. Railway network has rapidly expanded in Odisha. Since 2014 approximately 2200 km of tracks have been constructed. Full electrification has been completed in Odisha. 632 flyovers and underpasses have been constructed. Major projects that have been completed in Odisha since 2014 are many but Barang- Khurda Road 3rd line, Daitari-Bansapani new line, Haridaspur-Paradeep new line and Raitthagarh-Barang doubling are major achievements for smooth running of trains.

There is a long pending demand to construct a new railway line from Talcher via Narsinghpur of Cuttack district and Khandapada of Nayagarh district and connect it with Khudra Road-Bolangir line for alternate movement of coal from Talcher. Another demand was also to construct a loopline to Kantilo,which is a famous religious place of worship which attracts large number of pilgrims. This should be taken up urgently.

This year several rail projects amounting to about Rs 1439 crore have been sanctioned. Most of these projects were long pending demands of Odisha. They are- Badampahar- Kendujhargarh new line of 82 km with a cost of Rs 1876 cr, Bangriposi-Gorumahisani new line of 86 km with a cost of Rs 2269 cr, Bhadrak-Nirgundi 3rd line of 80 km with a cost of Rs 1284 cr,Cuttack-Nirgundi 4th line along with rail flyovers at Nirgundi about 16 km at a cost of Rs 759 cr and Nergundi- Barang-Khurda Road-Vizianagaram third line of 385 km at a cost of Rs 4963 cr to name a few. The Nirgundi-Barang rail line passes through Cuttack. Thererby, four rail bridges will be constructed over rivers Kathajodi, Kuakhai, Birupa and Mahanadi which will help decongest rail traffic in Cuttack, I Believe.

The internal revenue for 2026-27 is estimated to be Rs 3.02. lakh crore which is an increase of 8.4 percent over the revised estimate for 2025-26. The total revenue expenditure in 2026- 27 is estimated at Rs 2,99,500 crore which is an increase of 8.1 percent over the revised estimate for 2025-26. Capital expenditure in 2026-27 is estimated at Rs 2,93,030 crore which is an increase of 10.5 percent over the revised estimate for 2025-26. Budget support from the Central Government is estimated at Rs 2,78,030 crore financing about 95 percent of the capital expenditure. It is interesting to learn that Budget support in 2026-27 is estimated to be 10 per cent higher than the previous year. It is also learnt that the operating ratio is estimated to be 98.4 per cent which is lower than the revised estimate for 2025-26 of 98.8 per cent.

However, the ratio in 2025-26 was expected to be higher than the initial budget estimate of 98.4 per cent. As we know two-thirds of railway revenue comes from freight operations, 62 per cent of the total internal revenue in 2026-27 to be precise. Earnings from passenger train operations is at 29 per cent and sundry revenue at 8 per cent. Between 2017-18 and 2026-27, freight revenue has contributed an average of 68 per cent to total internal revenue, making it the primary source of revenue for Indian Railways.

Coal continues to be the single largest contributor to Indian Railways' freight earnings. In 2022-23, Railways had transported around 55 per cent of the total coal evacuated in the country. Coal consumption is projected to grow at about 3 per cent per year until 2030, translating into a cumulative increase of over 800 million tonnes. These factors are likely to sustain coal-related freight volumes over the next few years.

I would like to draw the attention of the Government regarding the Draft National Rail Plan-2030. It has observed that the rail freight charges are based on a minimum chargeable weight per wagon. This makes rail transport less competitive for light cargo, as charges are also linked to wagon capacity rather than the actual weight carried. Lack of time-tabled delivery for most freight trains also limits expansion into segments like e-commerce, parcel delivery and FMCG, where timely delivery is key. CAG in 2022 had noted that efficient management of wagons is crucial to achieve higher freight targets. This includes matching wagon availability with demand, better infrastructure and ensuring timely maintenance. Speed of goods trains is one of the vital indicators of efficient freight operations. Of late Railways have undertaken several measures to improve speed such as developing freight corridors, multi-tracking and monitoring freight movement across the network.

The problem today is, though freight cross-subsidises passenger services, it does not cover for all the losses from passenger services. Except AC 3 tier, all other classes of passenger services have observed losses.

A major share of Railways' revenue expenditure is budgeted towards staff salaries and pension. On an average Railways has spent 71 per cent of its revenue on salaries and pension in the last 10 years. Railways has remained a publicly owned and operated system. Private participation has been pursued through Public-Private-Partnership models and outsourcing arrangements. Several structural factors have constrained private investment in some railway infrastructure projects such as DFCs. As private participation has been limited because policy formulation, regulation and operations are all vested in the Ministry of Railways, it is high time these roles be separated.

Coming to quality of service, we may say poor punctuality and on-board cleanliness affect overall service quality. In 2022-23 over one lakh complaints were reported regarding non-availability of water in toilets and wash-basins on trains. Quality of linen was also enforced on contractors.

Last but not the least is safety. During the last 25 years, that is from 2000-01 to 2024-25, 984 consequential accidents have taken place. Consequential accidents are serious incidents such as collisions, derailments or fires.

Expenditure on safety-related works has increased from Rs 60,854 crore in 2017-18 to Rs 1,20,389 crore in 2026-27. Unmanned level crossings have been removed and Kavach system has been introduced. I would suggest the Government should consider ensuring equal access to travel safety measures for all railway passengers, regardless of the mode used to purchase their tickets. The Supreme Court has said there should not be a distinction. The passengers should not be deprived of travel insurance coverage for not booking their tickets online. Currently passengers who book tickets through the IRCTC website can opt for accident insurance by paying a nominal fee around 49 paise to Re 1. However, similar option is not available to passengers purchasing tickets at railway reservation counters. This distinction is difficult to justify. Method of purchasing ticket should not determine whether a passenger receives the benefit of travel insurance.

With the initiatives outlined in the Budget 26-27, Indian Railways is poised to play a decisive role in nation building by delivering faster connectivity, efficient logistics and resilient infrastructure in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat. Thank You.

SHRI RAJABHAU PARAG PRAKASH WAJE (NASHIK): I wish to speak on the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Railways for the year 2026-27. The government has presented this budget as a historic milestone for Indian Railways, highlighting large capital investments and modernization plans. However, if we move beyond the announcements and examine the ground reality, the situation appears deeply concerning. The financial position of Indian Railways remains fragile, safety concerns persist, passenger services continue to deteriorate, and several regions including my constituency of Nashik continue to face systemic neglect.

The financial health of Indian Railways raises serious questions. The operating ratio continues to hover around nearly 98 percent, which essentially means that for every ₹100 earned, almost ₹98 is spent on operational costs, leaving virtually no internal surplus for infrastructure expansion or modernization. A large proportion of railway revenue is consumed by committed expenditures such as salaries, pensions and lease liabilities. This clearly indicates that Indian Railways is increasingly dependent on budgetary support and borrowings rather than generating its own internal resources. If this trend continues, the long-term financial sustainability of our railway system will remain under serious stress.

Equally worrying is the issue of safety. The Comptroller and Auditor General has repeatedly highlighted alarming deficiencies in railway safety management. According to audit observations, between 2017 and 2021 India witnessed more than one thousand derailments, many of them caused by poor track maintenance and operational failures. Derailments continue to account for the majority of train accidents in the country. Beyond derailments, railway safety statistics reveal an even more tragic picture. Over the last decade, nearly 2.6 lakh people have lost their lives in railway-related accidents, including track crossings and operational failures. These numbers represent not just statistics but human tragedies affecting thousands of families across the country. Safety cannot be compromised, and yet the budget for critical areas such as track renewal and maintenance has not kept pace with the scale of the railway network.

Operational failures are also becoming increasingly visible. Audit reports and passenger grievance records indicate rising complaints regarding cleanliness, lack of water in train toilets, pest infestation in coaches and declining punctuality of trains. Thousands of signalling failures are reported annually in certain railway zones, which raises serious concerns about the maintenance of critical safety systems. While the government is focusing on showcasing high-speed trains and premium services, the everyday passenger travelling in ordinary trains continues to face discomfort and poor service quality.

Another structural issue that demands attention is the freight policy of Indian Railways. For decades, freight revenues have been used to subsidize passenger services. As a result, freight tariffs in India remain comparatively high. This has pushed logistics companies to shift a large portion of cargo transport from railways to road networks. Over the years, the share of railways in national freight transport has declined significantly, which is a strategic concern for the economy. When freight moves to roads instead of railways, logistics costs increase, fuel consumption rises and environmental impacts worsen. Instead of addressing these structural issues, the government continues to prioritize large announcements rather than deep policy reforms.

I must also highlight the persistent neglect of railway infrastructure in the Nashik region, which is one of the most important industrial and agricultural districts in Maharashtra. Nashik is a major hub for agricultural exports, wine production, defence manufacturing and pharmaceutical industries. It is also a major religious destination and will host the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2027, one of the largest religious gatherings in the world. Despite this importance, railway infrastructure development in the region has remained slow and inadequate.
 One of the most critical railway bottlenecks affecting the region is the Kasara-Manmad railway section, which is among the most congested corridors in the country. More than seventy trains pass through this section daily in each direction, and the corridor is operating beyond its designed capacity. Although the government has approved the project for the third and fourth railway lines between Kasara and Manmad, progress on the ground remains slow. This corridor is extremely important not only for passenger movement between Mumbai and Nashik but also for freight transport connecting central India with western ports. I urge the Railway Ministry to ensure that this project is completed within a clear and time-bound schedule.

Another important project is the Manmad-Indore railway line, which was sanctioned several years ago and has the potential to significantly improve connectivity between Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. This corridor can create new opportunities for agricultural trade, freight transport and regional economic development. However, land acquisition delays and administrative hurdles have slowed the progress of the project. The government must ensure that the project is expedited and implemented without further delay.

I also would like to draw the attention of this House to an extremely important issue concerning the Nashik-Pune Semi High-Speed Rail Project. This project has the potential to transform regional connectivity between two major industrial and agricultural hubs of Maharashtra and significantly reduce travel time, thereby strengthening trade, logistics and economic activity in the region.

In a reply given in this House, the Hon'ble Railway Minister, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, stated that the original alignment of the Nashik-Pune rail corridor had to be changed because of the presence of the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope observatory, and that the decision was taken based on technical advice.

However, a recent response obtained under the Right to Information Act from the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics has brought several important facts into the public domain. The RTI reply clearly states that the detailed technical reports relating to the GMRT observatory are extremely extensive and have not been shared publicly, and they are only available for inspection. This effectively means that there is no publicly available technical report or independent study placed in the public domain that conclusively justifies the decision to change the alignment of this major railway project.

Furthermore, the same RTI reply indicates that concerns related to the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope were first formally raised in November 2021 during a meeting with officials of the Maharashtra Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation. During that meeting, the Director of the GMRT observatory expressed concerns regarding possible radio-frequency interference but also suggested several technical co-existence solutions.

These included possibilities such as taking the railway line partially through tunnels, introducing electromagnetic shielding, or relocating the station slightly away from the telescope array.

This clearly indicates that changing the alignment was not the only available option. In fact, the scientists themselves had suggested technological solutions that could allow both the railway project and the observatory to coexist.

Across the world, there are several examples where radio telescopes and railway infrastructure operate in proximity with appropriate engineering safeguards. Therefore, it is a legitimate question whether these alternative technical options were seriously evaluated before the decision to alter the alignment was taken.

I would therefore request the Government to clarify whether a formal joint technical committee involving the Ministry of Railways, the Department of Atomic Energy and the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics was constituted to evaluate these options. If such a committee was formed, its report and recommendations should be placed before this House for the sake of transparency.

My intention is not to undermine the importance of this prestigious scientific institution operated under the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. The Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope is a globally respected research facility and a matter of national pride.

However, it is equally important that the interests of farmers, industries and citizens of the Nashik region are not compromised due to lack of transparency or incomplete evaluation of technical alternatives.

Therefore, I urge the Government to ensure full transparency in this matter and place the relevant technical reports, committee recommendations and the actual basis for changing the alignment before this House, so that any confusion surrounding this issue can be resolved and the people of the region receive clarity and justice regarding this important infrastructure project.

Another issue of concern is the lack of comprehensive railway planning for the Kumbh Mela to be held in Nashik in 2027. This event attracts millions of pilgrims from across the country and the world. Yet, there is no visible master plan for expanding railway infrastructure in preparation for this massive influx of passengers. The government must urgently initiate the expansion of Nashik Road railway station, develop additional platforms, upgrade passenger facilities and plan special train services to handle the expected surge in pilgrim traffic.

I would also like to draw attention to the challenges related to road over bridges and road under bridges in the Nashik region. In several places, poorly designed underpasses get flooded during the monsoon due to inadequate drainage planning, cutting off access for nearby villages and disrupting the movement of farmers transporting agricultural produce. There is a need for better coordination between railway engineers and local authorities to ensure that such infrastructure projects are designed with proper consideration of local geographical conditions.

In light of these issues, I urge the Railway Ministry to take immediate steps to address the concerns of the people of Nashik. The government must ensure the expeditious completion of the Kasara-Manmad third and fourth railway lines, accelerate the Manmad-Indore railway project, review and restore transparency in the Pune-Nashik semi-high-speed rail project, modernize Nashik Road railway station and introduce direct train connectivity from Nashik to major cities and pilgrimage centres across the country. It is also essential to prepare comprehensive railway infrastructure plan in advance of the Kumbh Mela in 2027. 

Indian Railways has historically been the lifeline of our nation, connecting regions, supporting economic development and enabling social mobility. However, for the Railways to truly serve the people, it must focus not only on grand announcements but also on safety, operational efficiency, financial sustainability and equitable regional development. The people of Nashik and millions of railway passengers across the country deserve a railway system that is safe, efficient, transparent and responsive to their needs.

Thank you.

डॉ. शिवाजी बंडाप्पा कालगे (लातूर) : मैं रेलवे मंत्रालय की अनुदान मांगों पर चर्चा में भाग लेते हुए सरकार का ध्यान महाराष्ट्र के मराठवाड़ा क्षेत्र, विशेष रूप से लातूर और आसपास के क्षेत्रों की रेल सुविधाओं की ओर आकर्षित करना चाहता हूँ । रेलवे देश की अर्थव्यवस्था की रीढ़ है और क्षेत्रीय संतुलित विकास के लिए मजबूत रेल नेटवर्क अत्यंत आवश्यक है । दुर्भाग्य से मराठवाड़ा क्षेत्र में अभी भी कई महत्वपूर्ण रेल परियोजनाएँ लंबित हैं, जिनके पूर्ण होने से इस क्षेत्र के विकास को नई गति मिल सकती है ।

सबसे पहले, लातूर - कुर्डुवाड़ी रेलमार्ग के दोहरीकरण का कार्य शीघ्र किया जाना चाहिए । इस मार्ग पर यात्री और माल यातायात लगातार बढ़ रहा है, इसलिए दोहरीकरण से रेल संचालन अधिक सुगम और सुरक्षित होगा ।

दूसरा, लातूर - बोधन, लातूर रोड - नांदेड़ और लातूर - कलबुर्गी इन नए रेल मार्गों को मंजूरी देकर इनके निर्माण कार्य को जल्द शुरु किया जाना चाहिए । इससे महाराष्ट्र, तेलंगाना और कर्नाटक के बीच बेहतर संपर्क स्थापित होगा और क्षेत्रीय विकास को प्रोत्साहन मिलेगा ।

इसी प्रकार लातूर रोड - परळी के बीच लंबित लूप/लैम्प लाइन का कार्य तत्काल पूरा किया जाना आवश्यक है, ताकि रेल संचालन में सुगमता आए ।

उदगीर में ROB (रेलवे ओवरब्रिज) तथा लातूर और लातूर रोड के अंडरपास का काम भी लंबे समय से अधूरा है । इन परियोजनाओं को जल्द पूरा किया जाना चाहिए, ताकि स्थानीय नागरिकों को सुरक्षित और सुगम आवागमन की सुविधा मिल सके ।

इसके साथ ही लातूर रेलवे स्टेशन पर पिट लाइन का निर्माण भी शीघ्र पूरा किया जाना

लातूर में प्रस्तावित रेलवे बोगी निर्माण कारखाना मराठवाड़ा के विकास के लिए अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण परियोजना है । इस कारखाने को जल्द पूरा कर उत्पादन शुरु किया जाना चाहिए और स्थानीय युवाओं को रोजगार के अवसर उपलब्ध कराए जाने चाहिए ।

भविष्य की दृष्टि से पुणे से हैदराबाद तक हाई-स्पीड रेल कॉरिडोर की लातूर मार्ग से विकसित करने का भी विचार किया जाना चाहिए । इससे इस क्षेत्र को राष्ट्रीय स्तर के आधुनिक रेल नेटवर्क से जोड़ने में मदद मिलेगी ।

इसके अलावा, लातूर मार्ग से उत्तर भारत और दक्षिण भारत के लिए लंबी दूरी की ट्रेनों की शुरुआत की जानी चाहिए, ताकि यात्रियों को बेहतर संपर्क सुविधा मिल सके ।

मैं यह भी आग्रह करता हूँ कि पुणे -सिकंदराबाद तथा पुणे - नांदेड़ (लातूर मार्ग से) वंदे भारत ट्रेन शुरू की जाए । इससे यात्रियों को तेज और आधुनिक यात्रा सुविधा उपलब्ध होगी ।

कोविड-19 के दौरान कई रेलवे स्टॉपेज बंद कर दिए गए थे । इन सभी स्टॉपेज को पुनः शुरु किया जाना चाहिए, क्योंकि इनका लाभ हजारों यात्रियों को मिलता है ।

इसके साथ ही ज्येष्ठ नागरिकों और पत्रकारों को दी जाने वाली रेल किराया रियायतें, जो कोविड काल में बंद की गई थी, उन्हें भी पुनः बहाल किया जाना चाहिए ।

मैं यह भी मांग करता हूँ कि बिदर - लातूर - CSMI सुपरफास्ट ट्रेन में आधुनिक LHB कोच लगाए जाएँ, ताकि यात्रियों की सुरक्षा और आराम सुनिश्चित हो सके ।

अंत में, क्षेत्रीय यात्रियों की सुविधा के लिए लातूर - पुणे तथा उदगीर - हैदराबाद मार्ग पर DEMU ट्रेन शुरू की जानी चाहिए ।

इन सभी परियोजनाओं और मांगों को यदि सरकार प्राथमिकता के आधार पर पूरा करती है, तो इससे न केवल मराठवाड़ा क्षेत्र का विकास होगा बल्कि देश के रेल नेटवर्क को भी मजबूती मिलेगी ।

इन्हीं शब्दों के साथ में अपनी बात समाप्त करता हूँ और आशा करता हूँ कि सरकार इन महत्वपूर्ण मांगों पर सकारात्मक विचार करेगी ।

धन्यवाद ।

MS. BANSURI SWARAJ (NEW DELHI): I am grateful to have been granted the opportunity to address this House during the Discussion on Union Budget 2026-27: Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways.

I wish to place before the Government the story of the transformation of Indian Railways over the past decade and the bold vision that will guide its journey in the years to come.

Indian Railways is not merely a mode of transport. It forms the circulatory system of our economy, moving millions of people, goods, and resources across vast geographic spaces and varied terrain with speed and efficiency. Historically, the expansion of railways has closely tracked every country's developmental trajectory: early networks enabled industrialization and territorial integration, while modern upgrades like high-speed corridors, freight corridors, and electrification support urbanization, supply-chain efficiency, and sustainable growth.

The last ten years have witnessed one of the most ambitious modernization drives in the history of Indian Railways. With a calculated policy shift prioritizing infrastructure creation, technological advancement, safety improvements, and passenger comfort, our Railways have transformed from mere transport infrastructure into strategic assets that our economy relies upon.

One of the most historic achievements has been the near-complete electrification of the broad- gauge network. Today, more than 99 percent of the broad-gauge routes are electrified, compared to a much smaller share a decade ago, cutting diesel consumption by more than 60 per cent since 2016. This transformation has reduced dependence on imported fuel, lowered operating costs, and made rail transport more environmentally sustainable. The effort has been recognised globally. The Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala received the Golden Peacock Award for Energy Efficiency 2024. Mission Electrification won the "Best Climate Change Adaptation & Resilience" award at the UIC International Sustainable Railway Awards 2022 in Berlin.

Safety, has been of paramount importance. The indigenous Kavach Automatic Train Protection System is being deployed on more than 2,200 route kilometres across the network to prevent train collisions and enhance operational safety. Developed by Indian engineers, this technology represents a significant milestone in our journey towards a safer railway system. Further, we renewed 54,600 km of tracks during 2014-26 to ensure safe train operations and tripled our safety expenditure from 39,200 Crore in 2013-14 to 1,17,693 Crore in 2025-26.

Capacity expansion has been pursued at a scale never seen before - 34,428 km of tracks were commissioned between 2014 and 2025, increasing the pace to 8.6 km per day. Over the last five years, Indian Railways has sanctioned 308 new railway projects, including new lines, gauge conversions and track doubling, with a total investment of around *2.93 lakh crore. There development works have been carried out to remove bottlenecks and increase the efficiency of the railway network.

The Indian Railways has also driven India's logistics transformation, under the Hon'ble Prime Minister's Gati Shakti vision. We have witnessed rapid growth of freight transportation through the development of dedicated freight corridors, and the Trucks-on-Trains Initiative. The operationalisation of the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor and the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor has already begun to change the logistics landscape of the country by allowing faster and more efficient movement of goods while freeing up capacity on passenger routes. Building upon this success, the government has proposed the East-West Dedicated Freight Corridor, connecting Dankuni in West Bengal to Surat in Gujarat. This corridor will pass through several key industrial regions and further strengthen India's supply chains and logistics network.

With regards to improved passenger experience, there have been major developments, including the digitalisation and automation of passenger services, making the passenger interface with the Railways simpler and more accessible. The introduction of the Vande Bharat Express trains, India's first indigenous semi-high-speed train, offer passengers a modern, comfortable, and efficient travel experience. These corridors support improved inter- city mobility, and easier migration. The Vande Bharat also marks a new chapter in India's Aatmanirbhar manufacturing capabilities.

Further, over 90 per cent Punctuality in 24 divisions of Indian Railways in this fiscal year with 19 divisions having punctuality between 80 per cent and 90 per cent, ensuring operational reliability and predictability. Over 80 per cent of the network is capable 110 kmph & above sectional speed, up from 40 per cent in 2014. Till date, approximately 12,300 coaches (including all operational rakes of Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat trains) & 460 locomotives, plying over IR's network, are equipped with CCTV cameras. At the same time, we are transforming railway stations into modern transport hubs. Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, more than one thousand railway stations across the country are being redeveloped with improved passenger amenities, enhanced accessibility, and better urban integration.

The last decade has also showcased India's extraordinary engineering capabilities through iconic projects such as the Chenab Railway Bridge, which stands as the world's highest single- arch bridge at 359, and the 11.2 km Pir Panjal Tunnel in Jammu and Kashmir, which is India's longest railway tunnel. Other marvels include India's first vertical-lift Pamban Bridge, the scenic Nilgiri Mountain Railway which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the rugged Konkan Railway route, and the Bhore Ghat section with 25 tunnels between Pune-Mumbai, highlighting immense skill and precise engineering across difficult terrain.

Freight continues to remain the backbone of railway finances. In the financial year 2026-27, the internal revenue of Indian Railways is estimated to exceed ₹ 3 lakh crore, with freight services contributing the largest share. At the same time, the government has made an unprecedented commitment to capital investment. The proposed capital expenditure of nearly ₹ 2.9 lakh crore will support the construction of new lines, track upgrades, safety improvements, and the induction of modern rolling stock across the railway network.

Looking ahead, the vision for the future is equally ambitious. The government has proposed the development of seven high-speed rail corridors connecting major economic centres such as Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Pune, Chennai, and Varanasi. These corridors, spanning nearly 4,000 kilometres, will represent the next leap in India's transportation infrastructure.

We are also mindful of the financial challenges that lie ahead. A substantial share of railway expenditure is devoted to salaries, pensions, and lease liabilities, and the implementation of the recommendations of the 8th Pay Commission may increase expenditure pressures in the future. Therefore, improving efficiency, diversifying revenue streams, expanding freight traffic, and strengthening financial sustainability remain critical priorities.

The transformation of Indian Railways is not just about laying tracks or running trains. It is about building a modern, efficient, and sustainable transport system that supports the aspirations of a growing nation. From electrification to high-speed rail, from freight corridors to modern stations, from network expansion to engineering marvels the journey of Indian Railways in the past decade reflects the confidence and capability of a new India. Today, the Indian Railways provides affordable Travel to 720 Crore passengers annually, making it one of the largest Government service providers across the world. With continued investment, technological innovation, and visionary planning, Indian Railways will remain a powerful engine of India's development and a symbol of national progress.

श्री मुरारी लाल मीना (दौसा) : मैं रेलवे अनुदानों की मांगों पर चर्चा में अवसर के लिए धन्यवाद करता हूँ । भारतीय रेल देश की सबसे बड़ी व सस्ती माल परिवहन व्यवस्था है, साथ में यह भारत के करोडो लोगो की जीवनरेखा भी है । विशेषकर गरीब व मध्यम वर्ग के लिए सबसे सस्ता व सुलभ परिवहन व आवागमन का माध्यम भी रेलवे ही है ।

रेलवे देश की अर्थ व्यवस्था की रीढ़ है देश में लगभग 68000 किमी रेल मार्ग है और ट्रैक की लंबाई एक लाख किमी से अधिक है । देश में 7300 के आस पास स्टेशन हैं और प्रतिदिन लगभग 2 करोड़ यात्री सफर करते है । 40 से 45 लाख टन माल की ढुलाई रोज होती है ।

जैसा मैंने बताया कि 2 करोड़ से ज्यादा यात्री रेल में सफर करते है क्योकि यह सबसे सुरक्षित व सस्ता साधन है । यात्रियों में 85 प्रतिशत से 90 प्रतिशत लोग अनारक्षित जनरल डिब्ब्बो में सफर करते है मात्र 12 प्रतिशत लोग स्लीपर और ए सी में सफर करते है । जनरल डिब्बों में सभी ने देखा होगा कि भूसे की तरह लोग भरे रहने को मजबूर रहते है । पिछले समय में सरकार ने स्लीपे व ए सी कोच को संख्या 190 प्रतिशत तक बढ़ाई है जबकि जनरल कोच की संख्या मात्र 15 प्रतिशत जिनमे गरीब जनता सफर करती है । आपने हाई स्पीड ट्रेने चलाई है जैसे वन्दे भारत उनमे आम आदमी सफर नहीं कर सकता है । मेरी सरकार से मांग है कि सामान्य श्रेणी वाले डिब्बे बढ़ाये जाये व साधारण ट्रेने भी चलाई जाये ।

रेलवे की वित्तीय स्थिति

वर्ष 2026-27 के लिए रेल मंत्रालय का कुल बजट लगभग ₹2.81 लाख करोड़ रखा गया है, जो कुल केंद्रीय बजट का लगभग 5.26 प्रतिशत है । इसके बावजूद रेलवे की टोटल आय का 98.4 प्रतिशत उसके संचालन पर ही खर्च हो जाता है तो बताये कि नई रेल लाइन व इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर के कार्य कैसे होंगे । जिनकी अभी बहुत जरूरत है, इस पर भी धयान दिया जावे ।

रेलवे दुर्घटनाः

2023-24 में 40 और 2024-25 में 31 गंभीर रेल दुर्घटनाएं हुई ।

NCRB की नवीनतम रिपोर्ट 2023 के अनुसार, 24,678 रेल दुर्घटनाओं में कुल 21,803 लोगों की मौत की रिपोर्ट की गई । रेल दुर्घटनाओं के कारण होने वाली मौतों की कुल संख्या 2022 में 20,792 और 2021 में 16,431 से बढ़कर 21,803 हो गई है, जो मौतों की संख्या में चिंताजनक वृद्धि का संकेत है ।

सुरक्षा के विषय में भी स्थिति चिंताप्रदः

सरकार द्वारा 'कवच' सुरक्षा प्रणाली अभी तक बहुत सीमित क्षेत्र में लागू हो पाई है । उपलब्ध आंकड़ों के अनुसार यह प्रणाली केवल लगभग 1,465 रूट किमी दक्षिण-मध्य रेलवे और लगभग 80 रूट किमी उत्तर मध्य रेलवे में ही लागू की गई है, जबकि NWR सहित पूरे देश का रेल नेटवर्क बहुत अधिक बड़ा है ।

हाल के वर्षों में रेलवे सुरक्षा कोष 45,000 करोड़ रुपये पर ही है । इसको भी बढ़ाया जाना चाहिए ।

अमृत स्टेशन योजना/पीपीपी मॉडल के स्टेशनो पर रोजगार समाप्त

सरकार द्वारा "अमृत स्टेशन योजना" के तहत रेलवे स्टेशनों का आधुनिकीकरण व नवीनीकरण किया जा रहा है । इस योजना के तहत कुछ स्टेशनो को पीपीपी मॉडल पर बनाया जा रहा है जिनका ऑपरेशनल गतिविधियों को प्राइवेट कम्पनियो को दिया जा रहा है इसका सबसे ज्यादा नुकसान माध्यम व लाखों गरीब परिवार जो रेलवे स्टेशनो पर थड़ी, ठेले, स्टाल व छोटी मोटी दुकानें संचलित कर अपने परिवार का पालन पोषण करते है इससे उनका रोजगार छीनने का कार्य किया जा रहा है । पहले इन दुकानों/स्टॉल के आवंटन में आरक्षण की व्यवस्था भी थी लेकिन इस योजना में आरक्षण का प्रावधान भी खतम हो जायेगा ।

रेलवे भर्ती व आरक्षणः

रेलवे विभाग ऐसा विभाग है जो सबसे ज्यादा सरकारी नौकरियां देता है । विभाग में करीब 16 लाख कर्मचारियों के पद स्वीकृत है जिसमे वर्तमान में 12-13 लाख कर्मचारी ही कार्यरत है । रेलवे का नेटवर्क बढ़ा है, कर्मचारियों के पद बढ़ने चाहिए । वर्तमान में करीब 6 लाख कर्चारी ठेके या संविदा पर लगे हुए है और 3 लाख पद खाली है । इसका सबसे ज्यादा नुकसान आरक्षित वर्ग को है ।

मेरे सरकार से मांग है कि खाली पदों व बैक लॉग को भरा जाये ठेके प्रणाली को समाप्त किया जाये या फिर उसमे भी आरक्षण लागू किया जाये । जबसे देश में भाजपा की सरकार आयी है आपने सरकारी नौकरियों को कम किया है, पब्लिक सेक्टर बेचते जा रहे है, बैंको का मर्जर कर दिया, जिससे सरकारी नौकरियां ख़तम होती जा रही है इससे ऐसा लगता है कि आप एक सोची समझी नीति के तहत आरक्षण व्यवस्था को ख़तम कर रहे है ।

रेलवे में नियमित कर्मचारी नहीं होने की वजह से, रेलवे की सचालन और सुरक्षा पर भी प्रभाव पड़ता है । इस कारण आधी से अधिक ट्रेनें समय पर नहीं चलती है ।

राजस्थान

राजस्थान के लिए इस रेलवे बजट में मात्र ₹10,228 करोड़ का बजट आवंटित किया गया है, जबकि राज्य में पहले से ही ₹56,863 करोड़ से अधिक की परियोजनाएँ चल रही हैं । इतनी कम राशि से यह स्पष्ट है कि पहले से चल रही परियोजनाओं को पूरा होना मुश्किल होगा ।

राजस्थान भौगोलिक और जनसख्या दृष्टि से बहुत बड़ा क्षेत्र है, उस हिसाब से बजट बहुत कम है ।

राजस्थान जैसे विशाल राज्य के लिए इस बजट में कोई बड़ी रेल परियोजना सम्मिलित नहीं की गयी, देश में प्रस्तावित हाई स्पीड कोरिडोर में राजस्थान को सम्मिलित नहीं किया गया जबकि जयपुर दिल्ली मार्ग पर इसकी आवश्यकता है ।

मांग 

मेरे लोकसभा क्षेत्र के बांदीकुई जंक्शन पर 700 बीघा रेलवे की भूमि पड़ी हुयी है । राजस्थान में सबसे पहले 1874 में आगरा फोर्ट से बांदीकुई ट्रेन चली थी । 1962 तक DRM/DSO ऑफिस बांदीकुई ही था जो ये जमीन खाली पड़ी है । मेरी मंत्री महोदय से मांग है की इस खाली पड़ी जमीन पर कोई रेलवे संबंधी उद्योग लगाया जाये ।

पूर्वी राजस्थान के प्रमुख धार्मिक स्थल मेहंदीपुर बालाजी, महावीर जी और केला देवी में हर वर्ष लाखों श्रद्धालुओं आते है । अतः बांदीकुई जंक्शन से मेहंदीपुर बालाजी, महावीर जी और केला देवी को मिलाते हुए नई रेल लाइन का निर्माण किया जाए । कम से कम मंत्री जी अपने रिप्लाई में इस रेल के सर्वे की घोषणा जरूर करें ।

दौसा से गंगापुर पिछले वर्ष नई रेल लाइन चालू की गई, जिसमे मात्र जयपुर गंगापुर एक डेमू ट्रेन चलती है । इसके स्टॉपेज बढ़ाये जाये एक डेमू ट्रेन इसी रूट सुबह गंगापुर से जयपुर व शाम को जयपुर से गंगापुर चलायी जाये तथा दिल्ली से अलवर दौसा गंगापुर कोटा के लिए इस लाइन पर ट्रेनों का संचालन किया जाए ।

दौसा जिला मुख्यालय है यहाँ से हजारो की संख्या में यात्री/ पर्यटक आते जाते है । दौसा जंक्शन पर वंदे भारत एक्सप्रेस व शताब्दी एक्सप्रेस ट्रेनों का ठहराव किया जाये । इसके अलावा बांदीकुई स्टेशन पर डबल डेकर, बसवा स्टेशन पर रानीखेत तथा बस्सी स्टेशन पर हरिद्वार एक्सप्रेस का ठहराव किया जाये ।

दिल्ली से जयपुर रेल लाइन पर रेलवे क्रासिंग जिन पर अंडर पास स्वीकृत नहीं है उन्हें भी स्वीकृत किया जाये ।

मीटर गेज के टाइम खान भाकरी और भंडाना स्टेशन चालू थे उनको बंद कर दिया गया है उनको चालू किया जाये ।अंत में मैं सरकार से निवेदन करता हूँ कि दौसा और पूर्वी राजस्थान की इन महत्वपूर्ण रेलवे मांगों पर गंभीरता से विचार किया जाए, ताकि क्षेत्र के विकास, पर्यटन और यात्रियों की सुविधा को बढ़ावा मिल सके । धन्यवाद 

SHRI LAVU SRIKRISHNA DEVARAYALU (NARASARAOPET): I wish to support the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Railways for the Financial Year 2026-27.

At the outset, I appreciate the Government for presenting a historic budget of 2,93,030 crore in capital expenditure for Indian Railways the highest-ever allocation for the sector, representing a 5.4 per cent increase over the previous year. I also note with gratitude the allocation of 10,134 crore to Andhra Pradesh, reflecting an eleven-fold increase compared to the 2009-14 average. This demonstrates the Union Government's firm commitment to strengthening railway connectivity in our state.

Under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji and the dynamic stewardship of Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw ji, Indian Railways is undergoing a transformation without precedent in its 170-year history.

The single most significant announcement in this Budget is the proposal to develop seven high-speed rail corridors at an estimated investment of 16 lakh crore. These corridors will fundamentally reshape India's inter-city mobility.

I wish to draw the special attention of the Government to the fact that four of these seven corridors directly benefit Andhra Pradesh. The Hyderabad-Chennai, Hyderabad-Bengaluru, Chennai-Bengaluru, and Pune-Hyderabad corridors form a "South High-Speed Diamond" that will pass through or terminate near Andhra Pradesh.

I thank the Ministry for ensuring that Amaravati and Vijayawada are integrated into the South High-Speed Diamond.

One of the proudest achievements of this Government is the indigenous Kavach Automatic Train Protection system. Kavach 4.0 has been successfully commissioned on 1,452 route kilometers. Over 4,154 locomotives have been equipped, 767 station data centres established, and more than 55,000 railway personnel trained on this technology.

Safety expenditure has tripled from 39,200 crore in 2013-14 to 1,20,389 crore in 2026-27, and consequential accidents have fallen by nearly 90 per cent. This is an extraordinary achievement.

However, I note that Kavach deployment has so far been concentrated on the Golden Quadrilateral and northern corridors. I strongly urge the Ministry to include the Vijayawada-Chennai, Vijayawada- Hyderabad, and Guntur-Guntakal sections of the South Central Railway in the next phase of Kavach rollout. These are high-density routes with heavy passenger and freight traffic, and they deserve the same safety protection.

The inauguration of the first Vande Bharat Sleeper Express on 17th January 2026 on the Howrah-Guwahati route marks a new chapter in overnight rail travel. With 12 Vande Bharat Sleeper trains planned for launch by March 2027, and 260 trainsets to be manufactured in total, this is a flagship programme.

I note that existing Vande Bharat services within the South-Central Railway zone including Vijayawada-Chennai and Secunderabad-Visakhapatnam are running at over 100 per cent occupancy. Vijayawada Junction is the fourth busiest railway station in India, handling 1.40 lakh passengers daily. Yet, Andhra Pradesh has not been allocated a single Vande Bharat Sleeper service so far.

I propose the following routes for Vande Bharat Sleeper services originating from Andhra Pradesh, and request the Ministry to examine them on priority:
 Route 1: Vijayawada/Guntur - New Delhi (~1,500 km)
 Route 2: Vijayawada/Guntur - Mumbai (~900 km via Guntakal)
 Route 3: Visakhapatnam - Bengaluru (~850 km)

Route 4: Vijayawada/Guntur - Howrah/Kolkata (~1,000 km)
 Route 5: Tirupati - Visakhapatnam (~800 km via Vijayawada)

I request the Ministry to allocate at least two of the planned 12 Vande Bharat Sleeper trains to Andhra Pradesh routes, with vishakapatnam to bengaluru and Vijayawada/Guntur-Delhi as the top priorities.

I make three specific demands to address this in the context of Andhra Pradesh:

1. The Government's Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal policy is excellent terminals have been approved, 118 commissioned, and ₹8,600 crore of private investment mobilised. I request the Ministry to sanction Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals in Palnadu district, which has significant cement, limestone, and agricultural output that currently moves entirely by road. The recently announced allocation of ₹14,500 crore for upgrading goods and parcel terminals must benefit our region.

2. Andhra Pradesh is a leading producer of chillies, cotton, tobacco, aquaculture, and horticulture products. The GCT policy already provides for cold chain infrastructure, warehouses, and micro-warehouses for e- commerce. I urge the Ministry to establish dedicated cold chain rail freight facilities at nadikudi, Guntur and Vijayawada to enable rail-based movement of perishable agricultural produce, which will reduce wastage, lower logistics costs, and boost farmer incomes.

3. The Budget has announced a new Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dankuni to Surat. I request the Ministry to plan feeder connectivity from Andhra Pradesh to this corridor, so that our state's industrial and agricultural exports to western India can benefit from this infrastructure.

The Government is rightly expanding private sector participation in Railways. Indian Railways is finalising a revised PPP policy with around 50 projects identified for private participation. The proposal to offer 50-year concessions to attract 35,800 crore in private investment for freight terminals and logistics hubs is a welcome step.

I request the Ministry to identify specific PPP opportunities in Andhra Pradesh particularly for station redevelopment at Nadikudi, Guntur and vijayawada under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, for multimodal logistics parks linked to the Dedicated Freight Corridors, and for private freight terminal development under the Gati Shakti policy.

I appreciate the Government's initiatives in AI-based ticketing systems, digital freight booking, CCTV expansion, and smart station technologies. I request that the stations under redevelopment in Palnadu district be equipped with modern digital amenities including passenger information systems, Wi-Fi, and CCTV surveillance as part of the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.

I wish to raise a matter of strategic importance that concerns the long-term financial health of Indian Railways before I conclude.

Today, coal alone accounts for approximately 50 per cent of total railway freight tonnage. Seven commodities together coal, iron ore, steel, cement, fertilisers, petroleum, and containers make up 87.3 per cent of freight loading. This over-concentration is a structural risk.

The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Railways has itself flagged this risk in its December 2025 report, calling for diversification into automobiles, FMCG, and e-commerce. A PwC study has shown that commodities with low rail modal share are growing at 10 per cent CAGR, while traditional rail commodities grow at only 5 per cent. If Railways does not capture this new freight, the revenue base will erode especially as India's renewable energy transition reduces coal demand.

At the same time, Railways' overall freight modal share remains at only 27 per cent meaning nearly three-quarters of India's freight moves by road, at higher cost and higher emissions.

Indian Railways remains the backbone of India's economic development and national connectivity. The unprecedented investments, the seven high-speed rail corridors, the Kavach safety revolution, the Vande Bharat programme, and the freight corridor expansion together represent a vision that will transform this country.

My appeal to the Hon'ble Minister is simple: Andhra Pradesh must not be left behind in this transformation. We need Vande Bharat Sleeper trains, Kavach deployment, Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals, cold chain freight infrastructure, and high-speed rail connectivity not as favours, but as investments that will generate returns for the entire nation.

With these words, I support the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Railways. Thank you.

SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE (DINDORI): I wish to participate in the discussion on the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Railways. I wish to draw the Government's attention to several critical railway issues concerning my Dindori Parliamentary Constituency and the surrounding Nashik district in Maharashtra.

​ Indian Railways is not merely a transport system but, it is the lifeline of millions and a powerful engine driving regional economic development. In regions like ours, where people are heavily dependent on agriculture, trade, and daily commuting, railway connectivity plays a pivotal role.

​ I would like to raise the issue of the Manmad?Kurla Godavari Express, which ran consistently for nearly 25 years, but has remained suspended since the COVID-19 pandemic. This train was extensively used by passengers for trade, employment, and education. I demand that this service be restarted immediately.

​ Regarding the Pune?Nashik Semi High-Speed Rail project, the Honourable Railway Minister, in a response to a starred question on December 3, 2025, stated that the original alignment via Narayangaon was altered due to objections from the Department of Atomic Energy and the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics regarding its impact on the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT).

However, information obtained under the RTI Act reveals that scientists had suggested several technical solutions, including diverting the route slightly away from the antenna cluster, shifting the Narayangaon station outside the protected zone, constructing tunnels in specific sections, installing electromagnetic shielding, and modifying railway communication systems.

​ These measures are globally accepted and have been successfully implemented in Europe and the USA. I urge the Government to clarify whether a detailed technical study of these alternatives was conducted before changing the original plan. If a joint technical committee was formed, its report should be placed before this House for the sake of transparency.

​ I also wish to draw attention to long-pending passenger issues at Yeola railway station. This station serves thousands of passengers from rural, tribal, and religious tourism sectors. I demand that the construction of Platforms 2 and 3 be completed at the earliest. Lifts should be provided for senior citizens, women, and differently-abled passengers. The Railway Reservation Counter, closed since the pandemic, must be reopened. A children's park should be developed on available railway land, and a high-quality RO water purification system should be installed. I also demand halts at Yeola for train numbers 12132, 22148, 11026, 12779, 11077, 22455, 17205, and 12129.

I also highlight issues regarding Lasalgaon railway station, which is at the center of Asia?s largest onion market. Before COVID-19, nineteen trains had official halts here, many of which were subsequently cancelled. I request the restoration of halts for Devagiri Express (17057/58), Shalimar Express (18029/30), Janata Express (13201/02), and Mumbai?Howrah Mail (12809/10). Additionally, Rajyarani Express (17611/12) and Janashatabdi Express (12071/72) should be given halts at Lasalgaon.

​ Regarding the Bhusawal?Igatpuri MEMU service (11119/20), this train remains idle at Igatpuri from afternoon until the next morning. This rake can be utilized to start an additional MEMU service from Nandgaon or Manmad in the morning to provide relief to daily commuters.

​ Manmad Junction is a major railway hub and requires attention. Rajyarani Express, Bhusawal?Pune Hutatma Express, Manmad?Igatpuri Passenger, and Tapovan Express should be operated regularly as in the pre-COVID period. At Nandgaon station, halts for Jhelum Express (11077/78) and Amravati Express (11025/26) should be restored, along with regular halts for Dhule Express and Sachkhand Express.

​ The Manmad Railway Workshop currently has only 600 employees against a capacity of 1,500, with over 200 vacancies. These posts must be filled immediately. This workshop should be assigned additional manufacturing and repair work to strengthen the Make in India initiative. Furthermore, the Health Unit at Manmad, serving 10,000 employees and families, should be converted into a full-fledged Railway Hospital. 

The foot over bridge near the loco shed should be reopened for employees. Also, the Kendriya Vidyalaya at Manmad should be expanded to Class 12 with more sections per class to accommodate children of railway staff.

​ Finally, regarding the 3rd and 4th railway lines, farmers must receive fair compensation for land acquisition. Alternative routes must be provided where traditional rural roads have been closed due to expansion. Proper drainage systems must be ensured in underpasses, such as the one at Nandgaon, to prevent waterlogging during monsoons.

​ These issues represent the genuine demands of the commuters, farmers, traders, railway employees and citizens of my constituency. I request the Honourable Railway Minister to look into these matters sympathetically and take the necessary decisions at the earliest.

श्री सुखदेव भगत (लोहरदगा) : माननीय सभापति जी, सरकार ने रेलवे के लिए 2.79 लाख करोड़ रुपये का आबंटन किया है, बजट बढ़ा है और यह सुनने में भी अच्‍छा लगता है लेकिन अगर ऑपरेटिंग रेश्‍यो को देखें तो ऐसा लगता है क‍ि दुकान में बिक्री काफी हो रही है लेकिन मालिक के पास बचत शून्‍य है । 

महोदय, सरकार ने आबंटन के साथ सपनों को सुपरफास्‍ट एक्‍सप्रेस बना दिया है, जहां घोषणाएं तेज दौड़ती हैं लेकिन ट्रेन अब भी प्‍लेटफार्म पर खड़ी है । अगर हम केपेक्‍स की बात करें तो पिछली बार की तुलना में दस फीसदी वृद्धि हुई है । अगर हम इंटरनल एक्‍सट्रा बजट रिसोर्सिस की बात करें तो 1500 करोड़ रुपये रखे गए हैं । आपने नए हाई स्‍पीड कोरिडोर घोषित किए हैं लेकिन इतने खर्च के बाद भी टिकट की लंबी वेटिंग लिस्‍ट, ट्रेनों की देरी और जनरल डिब्‍बों की भारी भीड़ कुछ और हकीकत बयां करती है । 

महोदय, भारतीय रेल दु‍निया का सबसे बड़ा नेटवर्क है जिसमें प्रतिदिन करीब दो करोड़ यात्री सफर करते हैं और 1500 मिलियन टन माल ढोया जाता है जबकि 2.7 लाख पद खाली हैं । यह गंभीर प्रशासनिक चुनौती है । अगर हम सेफ्टी कैटेगिरी, ट्रैक मैन्‍टेनेंस और गेट मैन की बात करें तो सारी चीजें इसमें समाहित हैं । रेलवे रोजगार देने का बहुत बड़ा नेटवर्क है लेकिन युवा बेरोजगार हैं और रेलवे जैसे संस्‍थान में लाखों पद खाली हैं । इससे तो ऐसा ही लगता है कि जैसे सरकार ने भी नौकरियों में रोजगार के लिए वेटिंग लिस्‍ट लगा रखी है ।

अगर हम ट्रैक इन्‍फ्रास्‍ट्रक्‍चर की बात करें, सिग्निलिंग सिस्‍टम की बात करें और टेक्‍नीकल स्‍टाफ की बात करें तो ऐसा लगता है क‍ि घोषणाएं तो बहुत तेजी से हुई हैं लेकिन हकीकत कुछ और ही है । सब लोगों ने रेलवे की बड़ाई की है, मैं भी आपकी सौम्‍यता और शालीनता की बड़ाई करता हूं । आपने रेलवे एप्‍स की बहुत हाई स्‍पीड रखी है । रेलवे आबंटन भाषण की तरह प‍टरियों पर तेज चल रहा है ।

आपने आधुनिकीकरण की बात कही है कि वाईफाई जोड़ दिया, यह किया, वह किया, लेकिन आज वस्‍तुस्थिति क्‍या है? यात्रीगण अपना मोबाइल 360 डिग्री पर घुमाकर नेटवर्क सर्च करते रहते हैं । आपने कहा कि बहुत आधुनिकीकरण किया लेकिन वस्‍तुस्थिति यह है कि अगर कोई ट्रेन टाइम से आ जाती है तो लोग उसके साथ सैल्‍फी लेते हैं और सोचते हैं क‍ि आज तो ट्रेन टाइम से आ गई । ऐसा लगता है कि सरकार रेलवे की नई स्‍कीम नहीं बल्कि लेट ट्रेन गारंटी स्‍कीम दे रही है । 

महोदय, रेलवे करोड़ों मजदूरों, छात्रों, मध्‍यम वर्ग के लोगों के लिए जीवनरेखा है । वर्ष 2025 की कैग रिपोर्ट कहती है क‍ि शौचालय और वाशबेसिन में पानी नहीं है, पानी की भयंकर किल्‍लत है और आपके पास एक लाख से ज्‍यादा शिकायतें आईं । एनसीआरबी की वर्ष 2023 की रिपोर्ट देखें, 24668 मृत्‍यु हुईं, जिनमें करीब 56 दुर्घटनाएं चालक की गलती के कारण हुईं ।

इसके अलावा, ट्रैक पर आपने 130 फीसदी ज्यादा लोड दिया है । इसके बाद भी हम अगर सोचते हैं कि घोषणाएँ बहुत आधुनिक और अच्छे तरीके से करे रहे हैं, लेकिन उद्घाटन तो हो रहा है और समाधान बाद में । लगता है यह आपकी कोई नई नीति है । साथ ही साथ, मैं माननीय मंत्री जी से यही कहना चाहूँगा कि झारखंड से इतनी बेरुखी और सौतेलापन क्यों? पिछली बार भी आपके इतने सांसद जीत कर आए और अभी भी बहुत सांसद जीत कर आए हैं, फिर भी झारखंड की स्थिति यह है कि आपने वहाँ कोई ट्रेन नहीं दी ।

​ मैं विशेषकर यह कहना चाहूँगा कि पूरे ईस्टर्न ज़ोन में, जो परमवीर चक्र विजेता का गृह जिला है, जहाँ अंजनी माता का स्थल है, जहाँ बाबा बैद्यनाथ और बाबा महादेव का टांगीनाथ धाम है, जहाँ आदिवासियों का सिरा सीता नाला है और जहाँ बॉक्साइट के भरपूर खनिज हैं । सारे मानकों के होने के बावजूद वहाँ रेलवे कनेक्टिविटी नहीं है । मैंने पिछली बार भी इसके लिए अनुरोध और प्रश्न किया था ।

​ अतः मैं विशेष विनम्र निवेदन करता हूँ कि इन पर ध्यान दें । साथ ही साथ मैं एक बात और कहना चाहूंगा जैसा कि कहा गया, हमारे वरिष्ठ नागरिकों, छात्रों और खिलाड़ियों के लिए कंसेशन की बात पर आप जरूर विचार करें । अंत में मैं यही कहना चाहूँगा सरकार कहती है कि रेलवे पटरी पर है, मगर यात्री पूछते हैं कि मेरी ट्रेन किस पटरी पर है यह तो हालत हो गई है? अंत में मैं यही कहना चाहूंगा कि

माननीय सभापति : ​श्री उत्कर्ष वर्मा मधुर जी । 

​ श्री उत्कर्ष वर्मा मधुर (खीरी) : धन्यवाद अधिष्ठाता महोदय, आपने मुझे रेल मंत्रालय के अनुदानों की मांगों पर चर्चा करने का समय दिया । ​

आदरणीय अधिष्ठाता महोदय, हमारे क्षेत्र लखीमपुर खीरी के लोग लंबे समय से बेहतर रेल सुविधाओं के लिए अब भी तरस रहे हैं । लखीमपुर, उत्तर प्रदेश का क्षेत्रफल में सबसे बड़ा जनपद है । यहाँ उत्तर प्रदेश का एकमात्र राष्ट्रीय नेशनल पार्क है और यह नेपाल की सीमा से सटा हुआ है । आज भी लखीमपुर खीरी की जनता अच्छी ट्रेनों के लिए तरस रही है । ​जनता की माँग है कि लखीमपुर, गोला और मैलानी स्टेशनों से होते हुए प्रमुख शहरों, राजधानी दिल्ली, हरिद्वार और अन्य राज्यों के प्रमुख शहरों के लिए एक्सप्रेस ट्रेनों का संचालन हो, ताकि नौजवानों, बुजुर्गों, महिलाओं और व्यापारियों को रेल आवागमन की सुविधा मिले और जनपद का विकास आगे बढ़े । ​पहले यहाँ छोटी लाइन थी, उसके बाद यह बड़ी लाइन हुई । जब छोटी लाइन थी, तब बहुत सारी ट्रेनें प्रमुख शहरों के लिए जाती थीं । लेकिन जब से बड़ी लाइन हुई है, तब से राजधानी के लिए या प्रदेश के प्रमुख शहरों के लिए एक भी अच्छी ट्रेन नहीं चल रही है,जो कि जनता की बहुत बड़ी माँग है ।

​ दूसरी महत्वपूर्ण माँग यह है कि हमारे जनपद में मैलानी से भीरा, पलिया और तिकुनिया होते हुए नानपारा तक जो छोटी लाइन है, पूरे जनपदवासियों की मांग हैं कि उसे बड़ी लाइन में बदला जाए । उसका अमान परिवर्तन हो जो हमारे जनपद के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है । वहाँ पूर्वांचल की बहुत सी आबादी रहती है जिनका अक्सर पूर्वांचल के जिलों में आना-जाना लगा रहता है, इसलिए यह बहुत उपयोगी लाइन थी । इसके अमान परिवर्तन की विशेष माँग है ।

​ हमारे जनपद के लोगों की एक और माँग है, जिसमें हमारे साथी सांसद (धौरहरा) श्री आनंद भदौरिया जी भी हमारे साथ हैं । हम लोग लगातार यह माँग कर रहे हैं कि गोला से मोहम्मदी होते हुए शाहजहाँपुर तक एक नई रेल लाइन बिछाई जाए, ताकि जनपद का विकास हो सके ।

​ इसके अलावा, गोला से अलीगंज मार्ग पर जो रेलवे क्रॉसिंग है, वहाँ एक आरओबी (रेल ओवर ब्रिज) की माँग है, क्योंकि वहाँ लगातार जाम लगा रहता है । खीरी टाउन और ओयल स्टेशन, जो हमारे जनपद के दो स्टेशन थे, उन्हें अब हॉल्ट बना दिया गया है । जनता की माँग है कि उन्हें पुनः स्टेशन का दर्जा दिया जाए ताकि जनपद का विकास हो सके । इसीलिए हमारे ​क्षेत्रवासियों की तरफ से मेरी यह पुरजोर माँग है कि दिल्ली और अन्य प्रमुख शहरों के लिए ट्रेनों का संचालन ज़रूर कराया जाए । बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद ।

श्री चंदन चौहान (बिजनौर) : माननीय सभापति महोदय, आपने मुझे रेल मंत्रालय के नियंत्रणाधीन वर्ष 2026-27 के लिए अनुदानों की मांगों पर बोलने का मौका दिया, इसके लिए मैं आपका आभार व्‍यक्‍त करता हूँ ।

महोदय, मैं विशेष रूप से आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी और माननीय रेल मंत्री जी का भी आभार व्‍यक्‍त करता हूँ कि उन्‍होंने स्‍वच्‍छ, सुरक्षित और एंवायरन्‍मेंट फ्रेंडली इंडियन रेलवेज बनाने के लिए जिस संघर्ष पथ पर चल रहे हैं, इस बजट में कहीं न कहीं उसी का प्रतिबिम्‍ब देखने को मिलता है । 

महोदय, वर्ष 2026-27 का रेल बजट भारत की तेज़ रफ़्तार से हो रही विकास-यात्रा का प्रतीक है । भारतीय रेल देश की अर्थव्‍यवस्‍था की मुख्‍य रीढ़ कही गई है । आज आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी और माननीय मंत्री जी के नेतृत्‍व में, इस वर्ष 2 लाख 81 हजार करोड़ रुपये के रिकॉर्ड बजट का आवंटन हुआ है । वहीं 2.93 लाख करोड़ रुपये पूंजीगत व्‍यय प्रस्‍तावित किया गया है, जो अब तक के सबसे बड़े निवेशों में से एक है । सरकार रेलवे के बुनियादी ढ़ांचे को मजबूत करने और यात्रियों को बेहतर सुविधाएं देने के लिए पूरी तरह प्रतिबद्धता से काम कर रही है । 

मान्‍यवर, जहां सभी पार्टियों के सम्‍मानित साथियों के विचार आये हैं, वहीं आदरणीय मंत्री जी, मैं तो यह कहूंगा कि माननीय अश्‍विनी वैष्णव जी पूरे देश में लोकप्रिय हैं । लेकिन मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र में सबसे लोकप्रिय मंत्रियों में से एक हैं । 

आज आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी और माननीय रेल मंत्री जी के नेतृत्‍व में विश्‍व के सबसे बड़े काम भारत में चल रहे हैं । चाहे चिनाब नदी पर पुल का कंस्‍ट्रक्‍शन का काम हो, 272 किलोमीटर लम्‍बा रेल कॉरिडोर बनाने का काम हो, 36 बड़ी सुरंगें बनाने के काम हों, 943 पुलों के बनाने के काम हों, टनल टी-50 बनाने का काम हो, नॉर्थ-ईस्‍ट में बैराबी-सैरांग रेल लाइन हो, रेल कनेक्टिविटी के क्षेत्र में देश का पहला वर्टिकल-लिफ्ट रेल ब्रिज, पम्‍बन बनाने का काम हो और पोर्ट्स की कनेक्टिविटी के लिए लगभग 42 परियोजनाएं चल रही हैं ।

इसके साथ ही, रेलवे की सुरक्षा बजट बढ़ाने का काम किया गया है । देश में यात्रियों का आवागमन सुरक्षित हो, इसके लिए 39,463 करोड़ रुपये के बजट को बढ़ाकर वर्ष 2026-27 के बजट में 1,16,470 करोड़ रुपये किया गया है । वर्ष 2013-14 में उपकरणों की संख्‍या बहुत कम थी, लेकिन आज उनकी संख्‍या 25,934 की गई है । 

डिजिटलाइज़, स्‍वच्‍छ और एंवायरन्‍मेंट फ्रेंडली रेलवे ने आज भारत को विश्‍व में एक बड़े पटल पर रखने का काम किया है । सरकार के द्वारा रेलवे के विद्युतिकरण पर काम किये जा रहे हैं । एआई, एनालिटिक्‍स एवं वीएसएस सिस्‍टम लगाये जा रहे हैं । 1731 स्‍टेशन्‍स पर वाई-फाई के साथ-साथ डिजिटल एसडब्‍ल्‍यूडब्‍ल्‍यू की व्‍यवस्‍था की जा रही है । 

उत्‍तर प्रदेश देश का एक बड़ा राज्‍य है, जहां यात्रियों का एक बड़ा नेटवर्क है । इस वर्ष उत्‍तर प्रदेश में विकास के लिए 20,012 करोड़ रुपये का बजट आवंटन किया गया है । मैं इसके लिए माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी और माननीय रेल मंत्री जी को धन्‍यवाद देता हूँ । वहीं पश्चिमी उत्‍तर प्रदेश, जो स्‍वर्गीय चौधरी चरण सिंह जी की कर्मभूमि है, में दिल्‍ली-मेरठ नमो भारत कॉरिडोर की शुरुआत की गई है, जो एक ऐतिहासिक कार्य है । माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी और माननीय रेल मंत्री जी अभी हाल ही में इसका उद्घाटन करके आये हैं । डिजिटल इंडिया और विकसित भारत का जो संकल्‍प है, उसे पूरा करने का काम आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी और माननीय रेल मंत्री जी के नेतृत्‍व में हो रहा है । 

मेरे लोक सभा क्षेत्र में तीन जिले- मुजफ्फरनगर, बिजनौर और मेरठ आते हैं । इन तीनों के शानदार रेलवे स्‍टेशन्‍स वहां मौजूद हैं । हमने और हमारे साथी चंद्रशेखर जी ने आपसे वंदे भारत ट्रेन के ठहराव की मांग की थी, आपने उसे भी करने का काम किया है । इसके लिए हम दोनों आपका आभार व्‍यक्‍त करते हैं । 

माननीय रेल मंत्री जी, मैंने आपको पहले ही बताया कि मेरे लोक सभा क्षेत्र बिजनौर में, हम सब से ज्‍यादा विश्‍वास...(व्‍यवधान)

आप हमारे यहां की सारी बातों का लगातार संज्ञान लेते हैं । मैं आपसे एक विशेष आग्रह करना चाहूंगा । मेरे यहां रोहनकाला स्टेशन है, बिजनौर में कोविड काल से पहले जो ट्रेन्स चलती थीं, ट्रेन संख्या 14521 दिल्ली-अंबाला छावनी इंटरसिटी एक्सप्रेस है, जो दिल्ली से अंबाला तक चलती है और जो साबरमती-योग नगरी ऋषिकेश योगा एक्सप्रेस है, अगर वहां पर इन ट्रेन्स का ठहराव सुनिश्चित कर देंगे, तो आपका बहुत आभार होगा ।

मान्यवर, महात्मा विदुर की धरती और प्रभु श्री कृष्ण जी की धरती हस्तिनापुर की एक लंबित मांग है, हम आपसे हस्तिनापुर से लेकर विदुरकुटी (बिजनौर) तक रेलवे लाइन बनाने की मांग लगातार कर रहे हैं, उसका डीपीआर भी बन गया है । जल्द से जल्द उसको पूरा किया जाए, तो अच्छा होगा । वहां के क्षेत्रवासियों की यह एक पुरानी मांग है । हमारे यहां चांदपुर और बिजनौर शहर में चार आरयूबीज़ और आरओबीज़ बनाने की आवश्यकता है । अगर आप उनका काम करवा देंगे, तो अच्छा होगा । आपने लगभग सारे काम पूरे करवा दिए हैं, ये आखिरी चार आरयूबीज़ और आरओबीज़ हैं । अगर इनका निर्माण भी हो जाएगा, तो वहां का यातायात सुगम हो जाएगा । 

महोदय, मैं अंत में कुछ कहना चाहूंगा । आज भारतीय रेल जिस परिवर्तन के दौर से गुजर रही है, वह वास्तव में भारत की विकास की नई कहानी है । माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी, आदरणीय रेल मंत्री अश्‍विनी वैष्णव जी और रवनीत सिंह जी के नेतृत्व में भारत में आने वाले समय में रेलवे यात्रा को और सुगम बनाया जाएगा, जिससे एक नया लक्ष्य बनेगा ।

महोदय, आपने मुझे इस विषय पर बोलने का समय दिया है, उसके लिए मैं आपको धन्यवाद देता हूं । मैं वर्ष 2026-27 के लिए रेल मंत्रालय के नियंत्रणाधीन अनुदानों की मांगों का समर्थन करता हूं । 

SHRI GOPAL JEE THAKUR (DARBHANGA): I am grateful to you for proving me an opportunity to express my views on Demands for Grants for Ministry of Railways. Under the leadership of accredited Hon?ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi- the Vishwakarma of modern India and the Hon?ble Finance Minister Smt. Nirmala Sitaraman for allocation of a praiseworthy amount of Rs. 2.93 crore for the financial year for expediting the pending works in the region. Hon?ble Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnav and his fellow minister of state Shri Ravneet Singh Bittu are motivating the railway workforce for historical developments and renovation work. I am thankful and grateful to them for this and hence I feel obliged on behalf of the State and the region. This would certainly approve execution of important projects and would expedite the ongoing projects. An unforeseen amount of Rs. This budget allocates ₹10,389 crore for connecting Delhi, Varanasi, and Siligudi with Bihar. Seven high-speed rail corridors have also been announced in the budget. It is a praiseworthy step on the part of Indian Railways. The first bullet train in Bihar runs between Varanasi to Siliguri via Patna. This initiative will greatly benefit travellers, and I sincerely thank the Hon?ble on behalf of the residents of Mithila, Bihar.

Sir, under the farsighted guidance of Hon?ble PM Shri Narendra Modiji and Shri Ashwini Vaishnavjee Rs. 1,09,158 crore has been allocated for renovation and upgradation work and such a huge amount was not allocated in the past and would be spent for execution and expedition of the historical projects undertaken for upgradation and renovation of railway stations, upkeep and maintenance with security arrangements. This would pave the path for lagging behind state of Bihar and even Mithila which was divided into two parts for lack of bridge. After 88 years, Hon?ble Minister for Railways Shree Vishnav felicitated the people with construction of a huge bridge in the region with an expenditure of Rs. 116 crore which could provide fast connectivity to around 8 crore people of Mithila in the state. What else could be a historical measure motivating the people for growth of economy, undermining the present one? A huge overbridge has also been constructed on the Koshi River. The doubling of the railway line spanning 225 kilometres between Darbhanga, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, and Muzaffarpur has been approved. I am grteful to the minister for this. I am also thankful to them for inclusion of a traditional dishes like Dahi-Chura, cuisine prepared with Fox-nut or Makhana being included in the menu in Railway Canteens for passangers.

A lot of railway crossings like Pandasarai, Laheriasarai, Donar, Bela, Museum have been falicitated with railway over bridge and I am grateful to the Hon?ble minister for this safety measures. 

Sir, I would like to raise some public demands. Railway halts like Shiso, Patharghatti be upgraded into Stations. Laheriasarai-Saharsa doubling of railway line be taken up at the earliest. Connecting the Mithila pilgrimage circuit to the birthplaces of historical figures can attract tourists and preserve local culture. A Vande Bharat train should run from Darbhanga to Delhi to help travellers.

श्री नरेश गणपत म्हस्के (ठाणे) : माननीय सभापति महोदय, मैं आपका हृदय से आभारी हूं कि आपने मुझे वर्ष 2026-27 के लिए रेल मंत्रालय से संबंधित डिमांड्स फॉर ग्रांट्स पर बोलने का यह महत्वपूर्ण अवसर दिया है । हम इस सदन में हमारी पार्टी के मुख्य नेता श्री एकनाथ शिंदे जी और गट नेता डॉ. श्रीकांत शिंदे की तरफ से अनुदान की मांगों के इस प्रस्ताव का समर्थन करते हैं । 

महोदय, जब भी भारतीय रेल के इतिहास का पन्ना पलटा जाता है, तो उसकी शुरूआत मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र ठाणे के जिक्र के बिना अधूरी रहती है । 16 अप्रैल, 1853 का वह ऐतिहासिक दिन, जब पूरे एशिया और भारत की पहली यात्री ट्रेन बोरी बंदर से ठाणे के बीच चली थी, तब ठाणे ने ही आधुनिक भारत की इस जीवन रेखा को सबसे पहले जगह दी थी ।

leaving trails of smoke across the sky;

कोयले की आग से चलने वाली यह आग-गाड़ी अब 100 प्रतिशत ऑटोमाइजेशन की तरफ जा रही है । 

इसका पूरा श्रेय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्‍द्र मोदी जी और रेल मंत्री श्री अश्‍विनी वैष्‍णव जी को जाता है । 

सभापति महोदय, रेलवे केवल एक विभाग या परिवहन का साधन नहीं है, बल्कि, इस महान देश की धड़कन और अर्थव्‍यवस्‍था का सबसे बड़ा इकोनॉमिक इंजन है । इस वर्ष रेलवे मंत्रालय का टोटल आउटले 2,78,030 करोड़ रुपये रखा गया है । इसके अतिरिक्‍त रेलवे के बुनियादी ढांचे को विश्‍वस्‍तरीय बनाने के लिए कैपिटल एक्‍सपेंडिचर केपेक्‍स को 2,93,030 करोड़ रुपये पर निर्धारित किया गया है । यह विशाल निवेश ओवरऑल रेलवे नेटवर्क को अभूतपूर्व मजबूती देने के साथ प्रोजेक्ट एग्‍जिक्‍यूशन की गति को कई तेज करेगा । 

सभापति महोदय, मुझे यह बताते हुए गर्व होता है कि वर्ष 2014-15 में रेलवे का ग्रॉस बजटीय आवंटन मात्र 32,300 करोड़ रुपये था । मोदी सरकार के निरंतर प्रयासों से वर्ष 2025-26 तक यह लगभग आठ गुना बढ़कर 2,52,200 करोड़ रुपये हो गया है । 

सभापति महोदय, अगर मैं अपने राज्‍य महाराष्‍ट्र की बात करूं, तो मोदी सरकार ने इस बजट में महाराष्‍ट्र पर विकास की बारिश की है । बजट 2026-27 में महाराष्‍ट्र को 23,926 करोड़ रुपये का रिकॉर्ड एलोकेशन प्रदान किया गया है । 

सभापति महोदय, यह आंकड़ा वर्ष 2009 से वर्ष 2014 के बीच यूपीए सरकार द्वारा महाराष्‍ट्र को दिए गए मात्र 1,171 करोड़ रुपये प्रतिवर्ष के औसत आवंटन से लगभग 20 गुना अधिक है । 

सभापति महोदय, जहां मैं इन उपलब्‍धियों की सराहना करता हूं, वहीं ठाणे लोक सभा क्षेत्र, जिसकी आबादी लगभग 26 लाख है, अपने प्रवासियों की कुछ महत्‍वपूर्ण मांगें और समस्‍याएं रेलवे प्रशासन के संज्ञान में लाना चाहता हूं । ठाणे रेलवे स्‍टेशन का अमृत भारत स्‍टेशन के तहत 949 करोड़ रुपए के एक मेजर अपग्रेडेशन का प्रस्‍ताव सेंट्रल ज़ोन द्वारा भेजा गया है, लेकिन, यह रेलवे बोर्ड में प्रलंबित है । इस प्रस्‍ताव को तुरंत मंजूरी दी जाए । 

Furthermore, a new railway station is being constructed between Thane and Mulund stations. Our Honorable Group Leader, Shri Shrikant Shinde?along with myself?had requested the Railway Minister, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, to allocate funds amounting to ₹250 crore for this project. I would like to specifically congratulate Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and, on behalf of the residents of Thane, express my gratitude to him for sanctioning this ₹250 crore grant.

This proposal has now been forwarded to the Railway Board, which is expected to grant its approval shortly, paving the way for the commencement of the station's construction work. On behalf of our Chief Leader, Shri Eknath Shinde?and in accordance with a proposal already existing at the state level?we hereby demand that this station be named 'Dharmveer Anand Dighe Railway Station. We formally place this demand before this House today.*

सभापति महोदय, ठाणे स्‍टेशन पर मुलुंड की दिशा में प्‍लेटफॉर्म नंबर 1, 7 और 8 को जोड़ने वाले एक एफओबी और प्‍लेटफॉर्म नंबर 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 और 10 पर एस्‍क्‍लेटर की तत्‍काल आवश्‍यकता है । कलवा-ऐरोली एलिवेटेड लिंक का काम तेज किया जाए और ठाणे रेलवे स्‍टेशन के प्‍लेटफॉर्म का विस्‍तार करके सभी ट्रेनों को 12 से 15 डिब्‍बों का किया जाए । 

सभापति महोदय, नवी मुंबई एयरपोर्ट टर्मिनल चालू होने वाला है, इसलिए, पनवेल स्‍टेशन से एयरपोर्ट तक स्‍पेशल ट्रेन कनेक्टिविटी दी जाए । 

सभापति महोदय, भयंदर और मीरा रोड स्‍टेशंस पर भारी भीड़ को देखते हुए चर्चगेट के लिए दो-तीन अतिरिक्‍त पीक-ऑवर लोकल ट्रेन्‍स चलाई जाएं । 

सभापति महोदय, भयंदर में बन रहे प्‍लेटफॉर्म की चौड़ाई कम से कम दस मीटर की जाए और टिकट खिड़कियां बढ़ाई जाएं । 

सभापति महोदय, दादर से जोधपुर के लिए वंदे भारत, दादर से अजमेर सुपरफास्‍ट 12989 को तीन दिन की जगह प्रतिदिन किया जाए । 

सभापति महोदय, जयपुर और जोधपुर की ट्रेन्‍स का भयंदर पर ठहराव देने का अनुरोध है । 

माननीय सभापति : अब आप अपनी बात समाप्‍त कीजिए ।
